The vehicle longitudinal and lateral kinematics was decoupled by feedback linearization method to be linear uncorrelation. Quadratic of longitudinal and lateral virtual accelerations are used as the optimal objective to reduces the fuel consumption. A decentralized optimization of longitudinal and lateral cooperative control method was proposed and the analytical solution considering the strict input constraint was derived. Efficiency of the proposed cooperative method was validated by simulation. The proposed decentralized merging control system can improve traffic efficiency and reduce fuel consumption with the potential for real-time application.

title: CLIP Distillation for Cross-Domain Traffic Scene Adaptation
authors: Hongyun Lu, Mengmeng Zhang, Zhi Liu, Hongyuan Jing
abstract: The adaptation of Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) models to traffic scenarios remains challenging, primarily due to three traffic-specific issues: heterogeneous feature distribution shift between general and traffic domains, severe label imbalance in traffic datasets, and insufficient attention to fine-grained local details critical for traffic scene understanding. To mitigate these issues, we propose a framework for fine-tuning the Chinese-CLIP model on specific tasks, integrating knowledge distillation and cross-modal alignment strategies. First, we introduce the Teacher-Anchored Margin Adaptation (TAMA) loss to support cross-modal alignment through teacher-guided dynamic margin constraints. This approach eliminates the need for explicit negative sampling and helps prevent model collapse by incorporating confidence-aware similarity regularization derived from teacher representations. Second, we adopt the Sliced Gromov-Wasserstein (SGW) distance as a distillation loss, which enhances cross-domain transferability by structurally aligning heterogeneous feature spaces. Additionally, we construct a multi-hierarchical traffic scene dataset, Hierarchical BDD100K (H-BDD100K), suitable for both global and local scenario modeling, and refine textual labels using large language models (LLMs) to improve semantic consistency. Extensive experiments on H-BDD100K and several other public benchmarks demonstrate that our method outperforms Chinese-CLIP baselines, maintaining competitive zero-shot generic scene classification performance while achieving a 7%-10% improvement in fine-grained traffic-related tasks.

title: Energy-Efficient and Perturbation-Aware Dwell-Recharge Integrated Strategy With Deep Reinforcement Learning for Catenary-Free Tramway
authors: Yixin Wang, Gaoqi Liang, Fengji Luo
abstract: Mounting global energy challenges necessitate a transition toward green and lean operational strategies across contemporary industries to bring eco-economic benefits about. This imperative extends to transportation systems, where emerging catenary-free tramways with novel onboard-offboard power supply architectures exhibit sustainable mobility while enhancing urban aesthetics. However, such systems still face critical challenges: simultaneous power demands during recharging cycles at stations risk destabilizing the tram traction power network, while mixed-traffic urban environments introduce operational vulnerabilities, manifesting as delays and congestion due to shared rights-of-way. To address these challenges, this study presents an integrated dwell time regulation and recharging scheduling method for catenary-free tramway, leveraging deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to balance dynamic energy demands with operational efficiency. The system dynamics are formalized through discrete event simulation (DES), and the decision-making process is formulated as an event-driven Markov decision process (MDP) to optimize real-time actions. The case study on a real-world catenary-free tramline in China demonstrates that our method can effectively diminish the peak power superimposition on local power network and the energy costs. Compared with representative heuristic and online optimization methods, DRL approach delivers a captivating solution for agile decision-making of intelligent tramway in the dynamic urban environments.

title: Applying Fused Data to Predict Vessel Traffic Flow: A Hybrid-Model Deep Learning Approach
authors: Wenchao Du, Tianyou Chen, Chong Ni, Yang Xiang
abstract: In the research on navigation efficiency optimization in complex waters, accurate vessel traffic flow prediction has emerged as a critical challenge in the field of intelligent maritime navigation. Based on Resolution A.1158(32) of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) and expert knowledge of Vessel Traffic Service (VTS), this study proposes a novel framework for vessel port reporting and VTS decision-making, and constructs a feature-fused database integrated with meteorological data. A hybrid deep learning model based on the DeepAR framework is developed, which extracts the spatial dependencies of vessel traffic via a convolutional neural network (CNN), captures temporal features using a bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM), and acquires long-range dependencies with a self-attention mechanism (SAM) to achieve multi-dimensional feature fusion for vessel traffic flow prediction. A case study is conducted on the narrow section of the Lüsi inbound waterway in Tongzhou Bay, China, to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can realize high-precision probabilistic prediction of vessel traffic flow. Compared with the benchmark methods, the proposed model reduces both the Mean Absolute Scaled Error (MASE) and the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) simultaneously for medium- and long-term forecasting ( > 24 hours) under specific working conditions (VTS six-shift mode). This study can provide probabilistic decision support for intelligent traffic management in narrow navigable waters, and serve as an important reference for VTS scheduling as well as port and shipping operation dispatching.

title: Point Cloud Mapping and Loop Closure Detection Using Superpoint Semantic Graph for Autonomous Driving
authors: Ronghua Du, Zong Li, Jinlai Zhang, Kai Gao, Lin Hu
abstract: Accurate loop closure detection and pose estimation remain critical challenges for autonomous vehicles operating in dynamic urban environments. While traditional single-vehicle SLAM systems effectively address the local “where am I” problem, achieving true global optimality and swarm intelligence in modern Intelligent Transportation Systems requires seamless cross-vehicle collaboration. To this end, we present a novel collaborative hierarchical framework that leverages superpoint graphs to achieve robust place recognition and precise pose estimation. Our approach begins by constructing a topologically meaningful superpoint graph, where nodes represent stable environmental features and edges encode their spatial relationships. For loop closure detection, we introduce semantic-enhanced ring descriptors that combine geometric structure with semantic information, enabling reliable place recognition despite viewpoint changes or temporary occlusions. The system employs a two-stage verification process: initial candidate selection through descriptor matching, followed by geometric verification using superpoint centroids with RANSAC-based outlier rejection. Crucially, abstracting dense point clouds into the SPSG format yields a highly compact data representation, making it ideal for low-latency transmission via V2X networks. By uploading these lightweight SPSG matrices and local pose estimations to a cloud server, our framework enables integrated global pose graph optimization across multiple vehicles, effectively overcoming the spatial limitations and accumulated drift of individual agents. Our overlap-based loop closure detection demonstrates superior performance across KITTI, Apollo, and Ford Campus datasets, achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) results on AUC, F1MAX, and recall rate. Furthermore, our pose estimation method exhibits consistently outstanding performance in both accuracy and robustness.

title: Entropy-Driven Adaptive Sensor Management for Non-Cooperative Multi-Object Tracking in Clutter
authors: Yun Zhu, Shuang Liang, Junkun Yan, Zan Li
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of adaptive sensor management in multi-sensor systems for non-cooperative multi-object tracking, where limited communication bandwidth and energy constraints must be balanced against tracking accuracy in dynamic and cluttered environments. We propose an entropy-driven framework for adaptive sensor management that optimizes both cardinality and spatial distributions under communication constraints. The approach uses a generalized labeled multi-Bernoulli random finite set model to characterize multi-object states and introduces two novel information-theoretic objectives: 1) minimizing the Shannon entropy of the cardinality distribution to reduce object number uncertainty and 2) minimizing the differential entropy of the spatial distribution to enhance localization precision. The problem is modeled as a constrained multi-objective optimization task. We prove the monotonicity property of the proposed multi-objective value function and devise an efficient decomposition strategy that transforms the global combinatorial optimization into tractable subproblems. The resulting entropy-based multi-objective optimization (eMOO) algorithm dynamically manages sensing resources while maintaining communication efficiency and estimation accuracy in non-cooperative tracking scenarios. Rigorous validation using simulation scenarios and a real-world taxi dataset CRAWDAD demonstrates that eMOO achieves superior tracking performance compared to the state-of-the-art method.

title: BSOEDet: Background Suppression and Object Enhancement Detector for UAV Aerial Imagery
authors: Shiliang Zhu, Bin Luo, Jun Liu, Zhensong Li
abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs), leveraging their flexible low-altitude imaging and real-time data acquisition capabilities, are widely employed for aerial imagery tasks. However, UAV aerial images contain numerous small objects characterized by low pixel proportions and weak features, making them interference to background noise. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a UAV Aerial Imagery Background Suppression and Object Enhancement Detector (BSOEDet). Specifically, an Object and Background Aware Feature Extractor (OBAE) was developed, in which an auxiliary region classifier differentiates between background and object regions, and self-attention and channel attention mechanisms are combined to suppress irrelevant background and enhance object features, thereby maximizing the representation of small object feature. Furthermore, we propose a Deep Semantic Mining Small Object Module (DSMSOM). DSMSOM employs cross-attention to establish cross-spatial semantic links between deep and shallow features. By leveraging scale-invariant features between large and small objects, and semantic correlations among different objects, it mines potential small object features in the shallow layers using the semantic information of deep large objects, and further reinforces these representations with Direction Adaptive Convolution (DAConv). Moreover, a Global–Local Object Distribution Aware Classification Loss ( ${\mathcal {L}}_{\mathrm {GLOD}}$ ) is incorporated, in which the average object area and number of the entire train dataset and each batch are statistically computed to dynamically generate classification loss weights, thus enhancing the optimization contribution of small objects and few-shot classes during training. BSOEDet is validated on the VisDrone and UAVDT datasets. n the overall performance metric $\mathrm {mAP}_{50}$ , BSOEDet achieves improvements of 6.5% and 9.4% over the baseline models, and on the small object performance metric $\mathrm {mAP}_{s}$ , improvements of 4.6% and 8.4% are observed, demonstrating the effectiveness and robustness of these proposed approaches.

title: Integrated Scheduling of Arrivals and Departures Subject to Sector Capacity and Route Topology in Terminal Airspace
authors: Ji Ma, Daniel Delahaye, Hong-Yan Zhang, Ruo-Shi Yang, Zhi-Qiang Feng
abstract: This paper presents an integrated approach for terminal airspace management which is limited by route topology and sector capacity constraints to improve arrival and departure operations. The study evaluates various arrival route topologies, including standard terminal arrival route, point merge system, vector for space, and trombone route, while departures are operated via standard instrument departure. A conflict detection and resolution mechanism is implemented for waypoint, link, and mixed-mode runway conflicts. A maximum capacity of the number of simultaneous flights within each approach sector is predefined, and sector congestion is monitored by precise entry/exit time tracking. An optimization framework is used to adjust speed, entry times, departure times and routing to minimize sector congestion, flight delays and extra flight distances. A tailored selective simulated annealing heuristic with local search is proposed to solve the corresponding problem. Computational experiments at Urumqi Tianshan International Airport show that the mixture of all topologies achieves the lowest average entry delay in terminal airspace (1.3 minutes), while standard and vectoring routes yield the lowest average landing delays (1.7 minutes). Point merge and trombone routes increase extra flight distances, while the mixture of three topologies achieves reasonable extra flight distances primarily through vectoring. Under nominal sector capacity, the mixture of three strategies continues to yield a lower average entry delay in terminal airspace. When sector capacity is severely restricted, the use of standard routes results in reduced in-sector flight times, though it requires significant deviations from scheduled time slots.

title: Multi-Agent Inverted Transformer for Flight Trajectory Prediction
authors: Seokbin Yoon, Keumjin Lee
abstract: Flight trajectory prediction for multiple aircraft is essential and provides critical insights into how aircraft navigate within current air traffic flows. However, predicting multi-agent flight trajectories is inherently challenging. One of the major difficulties is modeling both the individual aircraft behaviors over time and the complex interactions between flights. Generating explainable prediction outcomes is also a challenge. Therefore, we propose a Multi-Agent Inverted Transformer, MAIFormer, as a novel neural architecture that predicts multi-agent flight trajectories. The proposed framework features two key attention modules: 1) masked multivariate attention, which captures spatio-temporal patterns of individual aircraft; and 2) agent attention, which models the social patterns among multiple agents in complex air traffic scenes. We evaluated MAIFormer using a real-world automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast flight trajectory dataset from the terminal airspace of Incheon International Airport in South Korea. The experimental results show that MAIFormer achieves the best performance across multiple metrics and outperforms other methods. In addition, MAIFormer produces prediction outcomes that are interpretable from a human perspective, which improves both the transparency of the model and its practical utility in air traffic control.

title: An Explainable KAN--Shapley Framework for Many-to-Many Electric Vehicle Charging Dispatch in Intelligent Transportation Systems
authors: Wen-Dong Jiang, Chih-Yung Chang, Tzu-Chia Huang, Yue-Shi Lee, Diptendu Sinha Roy
abstract: Mobile Charging Services (MCS) can alleviate the shortage of fixed charging infrastructure, but real-world dispatching in dense cities must jointly handle time-varying traffic and grid-price signals, hard feasibility constraints such as SOC safety, service time windows, and service regions, and the need for auditable decisions. Existing optimization-based schedulers rely on hand-crafted costs and provide limited decision transparency, whereas end-to-end learning-based dispatchers are often opaque and may violate constraints at inference time. This paper proposes an Explainable KAN–Shapley Dispatch Network (XKSDN) for many-to-many dispatch between EV charging request clusters and multiple Mobile Charging Vehicles (MCVs). XKSDN first abstracts massive requests via spatiotemporal–energy clustering, and then learns a structured utility function with a Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN), whose edge-wise one-dimensional spline functions expose nonlinear effects such as distance decay and SOC-urgency transitions. To turn learned utilities into executable schedules, a constraint-aware matching layer integrates feasibility masking (Big- $M$ ), virtual nodes for partial matching, and node replication for limited MCV capacity, and solves the resulting assignment with an improved Hungarian algorithm. For accountability, XKSDN computes local Shapley-value attributions within clusters, quantifying the marginal contributions of distance, SOC, congestion, and price to each dispatch command. Experiments on New York City trip data with SUMO simulations show that XKSDN improves service success rate and response delay while reducing operational cost against representative optimization and deep learning baselines, and provides consistent, auditable explanations for safety-critical deployments.

title: Optimizing Bus Stop Operations Within ITS: Dynamic Stop Zone Allocation
authors: Qiaowen Bai, Fang Zhang, Chien-Ming Chen, Jinhao Liang, Mohammed Amoon
abstract: Advances in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) offer new opportunities to enhance bus stop operations and transit system reliability. This need is particularly relevant for staggered bus stops, which consist of multiple stop zones (each serving specific bus services and comprising one or more berths) and are prone to bus stop failures due to suboptimal allocation of bus services to stop zones. However, existing studies in this field remain limited, especially in addressing real-time dynamic allocation with practical considerations. To fill this gap, we introduce an overlap prediction-based approach for real-time optimal allocation of stop zones to bus services within staggered bus stop configuration. Firstly, a LightGBM-based overlap prediction model is developed to estimate the probability of simultaneous arrivals by buses from different services, using real-time operational data. Then, an integer linear programming model is formulated to achieve optimal bus service allocation by minimizing overlap costs, while accounting for an allocation consistency constraint to reduce frequent changes in stop zone assignments for the same bus service. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using real-world data in Singapore. Sensitivity analyses are conducted to assess the model’s robustness and reliability by examining the impacts of time interval and maximum permitted stop zone change count. The proposed method offers transit agencies and operators a practical solution for dynamic stop zone allocation at staggered bus stops, improving service quality within ITS environments.

title: Problem-Specific Knowledge and Learning-Based Meta-Heuristics for On-Demand Food Delivery Scheduling
authors: Yaxian Ren, Kaizhou Gao, Zhongjie Lin, Naiqi Wu, Ling Wang, Liang Zhao
abstract: With the increase of orders and riders, how to allocate orders to riders appropriately and complete delivery timely are huge challenges in on-demand food delivery (OFD). This work focuses on the multi-objective on-demand food delivery scheduling problems (OFDSP) with minimizing the total delay time of all orders and the total traveling distance of all riders simultaneously. First, both order-based mathematical model and a location-based mathematical model are established for the concerned problems, respectively Then, three basic algorithms (differential evolution (DE), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and artificial bee colony (ABC)) are improved to solve OFDSP. Combining order and rider information, a double string encoding method is designed to represent candidate solutions. A multi-constraint satisfying initialization strategy is proposed to avoid infeasible solutions. Seven problem-specific knowledge-based local search operators (KLSOs) are developed to speed up the convergence of the algorithms. Third, two reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms with two Q-table design strategies are constructed, yielding a total of four RL-based strategies for local search operator selection during iterations. Finally, 30 instances from real scenarios are solved to verify the performance of the proposed algorithms. The two developed mathematical models are verified and compared. The effectiveness of the improvement strategies is validated in the respective algorithm groups. Furthermore, the algorithms with the best performance in the respective groups are compared to the two advanced OFD algorithms. The results and comparisons show that the ABC_LS_Q1 is most competitive among all compared algorithms.

title: Improving Traffic Sign Detection Under Adverse Snowy Environments via Frequency-Enhanced EfficientViT
authors: Yuhuan Wang, Tingting Wang, Yuan Wang, Tieji Zhang, Yunfeng Hu

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Intelligent Transportation Systems: A Survey on Architecture, Use Cases, and Future Directions
authors: Mohamed EL Amine Ameur, Bouziane Brik, Habiba Drias, Mazene Ameur, Sebti Foufou, Albert Zomaya
abstract: The emergence of Cooperative Intelligent Transportation Systems (C-ITS) has revolutionized urban mobility by enabling seamless collaboration among vehicles, infrastructure, and individuals to improve traffic management, safety, and efficiency. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has become a key technology in this ecosystem, empowering autonomous agents to make real-time decisions that optimize traffic flow, reduce congestion, and enhance road safety. Although many surveys on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) either overlook cooperative aspects or primarily emphasize security, this paper bridges the gap by examining the diverse applications of DRL in C-ITS. It examines critical areas such as traffic signal control, AV coordination, route planning, and human-vehicle interaction. The study also traces the evolution of DRL algorithms, their adaptation to transportation challenges, and their integration with cutting-edge projects and standards. Additionally, the paper provides a comprehensive analysis of current research trends, identifying achievements, unresolved challenges, and future directions in the field. By synthesizing existing literature and highlighting the synergy between DRL and C-ITS, this survey serves as a valuable resource for researchers, policymakers, and industry professionals striving to develop intelligent, cooperative, and sustainable transportation systems. The insights offered aim to guide advancements in this rapidly growing domain, fostering innovation and practical implementation.

title: Interdependent Microservice Offloading and Semantic Aware Results Transmission for 6G Vehicular Edge Networks
authors: Muhammad Salah ud din, Muhammad Nadeem Ali, Ghulam Musa Raza, Muhammad Imran, Byung-Seo Kim

title: A Real-Time Adaptive Map Matching Algorithm for Diverse Road Scenarios
authors: Yan Feng, Ying Wang, Gongju Guo, Weiwei Zhang, Jin Zhu
abstract: Map matching in this study refers to the process of aligning vehicle trajectory data (e.g., GPS observations) with a digital road network. It is a key technique in the fields of intelligent transportation systems (ITS) and autonomous driving. However, existing methods still face considerable challenges in diverse road scenarios, such as intersections, steep slopes with sharp curves, and elevated roads. This study aims to improve matching accuracy in diverse road scenarios while maintaining real-time performance. It also addresses map matching in road segments with similar planar alignments but different elevations. To address these challenges, we propose the Real-Time Adaptive Map Matching Algorithm (RAM). RAM incorporates a moving window mechanism to retain locally relevant trajectory points, thereby improving computational efficiency for real-time applications. Furthermore, RAM leverages both road geometric features and topological information to construct adaptive matching functions for different road scenarios. In addition, the algorithm incorporates trajectory deviation compensation and elevation-difference handling. This design improves robustness in scenarios involving signal loss and elevation-differential road segments. The proposed algorithm was evaluated on representative road segments covering diverse road scenarios. The performance of the RAM algorithm was evaluated based on two primary metrics: matching accuracy and real-time processing efficiency. Experimental results show that RAM achieves a favorable balance between matching accuracy and real-time processing efficiency through the moving window mechanism, error-ellipse constraint, and adaptive feature matching strategy. The paper also provides a detailed analysis of the algorithm’s time complexity, emphasizing its strengths in terms of real-time performance and matching precision. The proposed method provides an effective solution for trajectory-to-road map matching in intelligent transportation and autonomous driving applications.

title: SDATNet: Social Diverse Adaptive TrajectorNet for Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction Under Long-Tail Behavior Distributions
authors: Zihan Jiang, Ruonan Liu, Xiuzhong Hu, Yafeng Guo, Weidong Zhang
abstract: Pedestrian trajectory prediction is vital for safety-critical applications such as autonomous driving and video surveillance. While recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved predictive accuracy, most models struggle with underrepresented and diverse behaviors present in the long-tail distribution of pedestrian trajectories. To address this challenge, we propose Social Diverse Adaptive TrajectorNet (SDATNet), a novel deep learning framework designed to enhance prediction performance on rare and atypical trajectory patterns. SDATNet introduces three key innovations: 1) the ResGhost module, which incorporates residual connections and ghost operations to enrich multi-scale social feature diversity; 2) a Dynamic Weights Variety Loss (DWVL) that adaptively emphasizes rare behaviors by weighting loss based on prediction uncertainty; and 3) an Adaptive Gaussian Distribution module that stabilizes the modeling of outlier trajectories by aligning prediction distributions with behavioral variance. The results demonstrate that the SDATNet outperforms existing methods in predicting pedestrian trajectories, offering a reliable and versatile solution for real-world applications.

title: Lifelong Learner: Discovering Versatile Neural Solvers for Vehicle Routing Problems
authors: Shaodi Feng, Zhuoyi Lin, Jianan Zhou, Cong Zhang, Jingwen Li, Kuan-Wen Chen, Senthilnath Jayavelu, Yew-Soon Ong
abstract: Deep learning has been increasingly adopted in intelligent transportation systems (ITS) to address vehicle routing problems (VRPs) that arise in real-world operations such as fleet management, urban logistics, and dynamic dispatching. However, most neural solvers are trained to tackle VRP instances in a relatively monotonous context, e.g., simplifying VRPs by using Euclidean distance between nodes and adhering to a single problem size, which harms their off-the-shelf application in different scenarios. To enhance their versatility, this paper presents a novel lifelong learning framework that incrementally trains a neural solver to manage VRPs in distinct contexts. Specifically, we propose a lifelong learner (LL), exploiting a Transformer network as the backbone, to solve a series of VRPs. The inter-context self-attention mechanism is proposed within LL to transfer the knowledge obtained from solving preceding VRPs into the succeeding ones. On top of that, we develop a dynamic context scheduler (DCS), employing the cross-context experience replay to further facilitate LL looking back on the attained policies of solving preceding VRPs. Extensive results on synthetic and benchmark instances (problem sizes up to 18k) show that our LL is capable of discovering effective policies for tackling generic VRPs in varying contexts. The source code is available: https://github.com/fsdfsd123/Lifelong-Learner-Discovering-More-Versatile-Neural-Solvers-for-Routing-Problems.

title: Hybrid Frame-Enhanced LiDAR/GNSS/IMU Fusion for Accurate and Robust Mapping in Mixed Traffic Environments
authors: Yunshui Zhou, Hongmao Qin, Dengxiang Chang, Runbang Zhang, Shengjie Huang, Yougang Bian, Manjiang Hu

title: Exploiting Formal Verification for the Systematic Discovery of Corner Cases in a Behavior Planner for Automated Driving
authors: Lukas Konig, Franziska Henze, Christian Heinzemann, Michaela Klauck, Alberto Griggio, Stefano Tonetta, Alessandro Cimatti
abstract: In automated driving, preventing hazardous driving decisions is both an extremely important and intricate task. Typical verification and validation methods include extensive simulation and real-world testing which is expensive and, yet, cannot rule out rare but potentially hazardous corner cases. Therefore, we present an approach to enhance the verification and validation process of automated driving by applying formal verification techniques for bug finding directly to the code of a tactical behavior planner in series development. We use an open source software framework in combination with the model checker nuXmv. Our framework involves fully automatically extracting the model from C++ code, integrating it with a traffic simulator, and conducting exhaustive analysis over a broad range of possible traffic scenes using model checking. If violations, e. g., crashes, are detected, traces of the surrounding traffic participants and ego are obtained, which can be simulated with the full system to aid in error identification, or utilized to generate corner cases for conventional testing. Since model checking is usually runtime-intensive, we analyze the effects of different discretization step sizes for time and space. Our results show that the toolchain identifies formerly unknown bugs in a real series development, even with surprisingly coarse discretizations. This demonstrates that model checking can improve the development process of industrial ADAS projects.

title: Driving Style Recognition Like an Expert Using Semantic Privileged Information From Large Language Models
authors: Zhaokun Chen, Chaopeng Zhang, Xiaohan Li, Wenshuo Wang, Gentiane Venture, Junqiang Xi
abstract: Existing driving style recognition systems largely depend on low-level sensor-derived features for training, neglecting the rich semantic reasoning capability inherent to human experts. This discrepancy results in a fundamental misalignment between algorithmic classifications and expert judgments. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel framework that integrates Semantic Privileged Information (SPI) derived from large language models (LLMs) to align recognition outcomes with human-interpretable reasoning. First, we introduce DriBehavGPT, an interactive LLM-based module that generates natural-language descriptions of driving behaviors. These descriptions are then encoded into machine learning-compatible representations via text embedding and dimensionality reduction. Finally, we incorporate them as privileged information into Support Vector Machine Plus (SVM+) for training, enabling the model to approximate human-like interpretation patterns. Experiments across diverse real-world driving scenarios demonstrate that our SPI-enhanced framework consistently outperforms a wide range of baselines, achieving $F_{1}$ -scores of 90.2% (car-following) and 91.0% (lane-changing). Importantly, SPI is exclusively used during training, while inference relies solely on sensor data, ensuring computational efficiency without sacrificing performance. These results highlight the pivotal role of semantic behavioral representations in improving recognition accuracy while advancing interpretable, human-centric driving systems.

title: AutoLegal: Toward Universal Traffic Compliance for Autonomous Vehicles Through Knowledge-Enhanced Language Models and Signal Temporal Logic
authors: Shunran Zhang, Huiyun Li, Zhengmin Jiang, Ming Sang, Jindai Liu, Leong Hou U
abstract: Compliance verification of autonomous vehicle behavior represents a fundamental requirement for transportation system deployment. While human drivers handle natural language ambiguities intuitively, autonomous vehicles require precise formal specifications to eliminate linguistic uncertainties and ensure compliance. However, global traffic regulations exhibit substantial variations, creating significant challenges for formal specification languages in representing diverse natural language regulations across jurisdictions. Current approaches face critical limitations: manual formalization methods are labor-intensive and lack cross-regional adaptability, while existing Large Language Model (LLM)-based translation methods suffer from limited representability of traffic concept semantics and generate incorrect representations of temporal constraints and logical relationships due to insufficient reasoning accuracy. This paper presents AutoLegal, a novel translation framework leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) for systematic traffic regulation formalization. The framework integrates semantic foundations with knowledge graphs to provide LLMs with semantic anchors that ensure representability guarantees and atomic predicate consistency. To address logical reasoning demands, the framework incorporates explicit tree-structured logical expressions within Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, transforming implicit reasoning into interpretable and verifiable processes for enhanced temporal-logical relationship handling. A dual verification mechanism combining syntax validation and semantic back-translation validation with iterative refinement ensures final output quality and system robustness. Experimental results validate AutoLegal’s capability for translating traffic regulations into Signal Temporal Logic, achieving a translation success rate of 73.7% that surpasses other LLM-based methods, while the coverage of rule representations exceeds manual translation. Analysis of atomic predicate semantic representation performance and large language model hallucination mitigation capabilities further explains AutoLegal’s superior performance. The generated STL specifications demonstrate verified monitorability and semantic accuracy in real-world scenarios, thereby facilitating the advancement of intelligent transportation systems.

title: GATEWAY: A Game Theory Model for Analyzing NYC Road Tolls and Commuter Response
authors: Hailun Wu, Ziqian Dong, Roberto Rojas-Cessa
abstract: Road toll policies, such as the newly implemented congestion pricing in New York City, are effective measures in both reducing traffic congestion and generating revenue. However, pursuing these two objectives requires understanding how toll policy changes influence commuters’ travel mode choices. Existing tools aim to estimate car travel demand but overlook the trade-off between traffic reduction and revenue generation. To address this gap, we propose GATEWAY, a Stackelberg game-based model where a policymaker introduces a toll, and commuters respond to the toll by selecting a travel mode. By identifying the Nash equilibrium, where the objectives of the policymaker and the commuters travel mode choice are optimized, GATEWAY suggests a toll and estimates the respective travel demand. The accuracy of GATEWAY was validated through two case studies: the New York City’s bridge and tunnel toll increase in 2010 and the congestion pricing program implemented in 2025. Our results show high consistency in the estimation of car travel demand and consumer surplus compared to the actual traffic volume reported by the Metropolitan Transportation Authority and a transportation-policy multi-agent virtual testbed, respectively. GATEWAY can also predict the reduction in traffic and the revenue generation of future toll increases.

title: ByFeDis: Toward Byzantine-Robust Heterogeneous Federated Learning via Knowledge Distillation in Railway Intelligent Control Systems
authors: Shijia Guo, Rong Sun, Jingwei Liu

title: A Hierarchical Control Framework for Platoon-Based Connected Autonomous Vehicles in Congested Ramp Merging Areas
authors: Yixuan Wang, Shunying Zhu, Hao Zhang
abstract: To improve traffic efficiency in congested ramp merging areas, this study proposes a hierarchical platoon-based control framework for connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs). The upper layer serves as the macroscopic decision-making layer and adopts a centralized control approach, where a threshold-rule is used for platoon formation. Subsequently, we employ a dynamic method that triggers updates based on events and solve an optimization model in real-time to determine the assigned arrival times of platoons at the merge point, which are then used to establish the merging sequence. The lower layer serves as the microscopic planning layer and adopts a distributed control approach. It applies optimal control theory to derive online closed-form analytical solutions for intra-platoon and inter-platoon trajectory planning, explicitly targeting improvements in energy efficiency, ride comfort. The numerical results show that, compared to the other three strategies, the proposed method achieves significant improvements. The associated codes are accessible at https://ieee-dataport.org/documents/hierarchical-control-framework-platoon-based-connected-autonomous-vehicles-congested-ramp

title: IDGM-DD: Interactive Decision-Making Model for Autonomous Vehicles Integrating Dynamic Game Theory and Driving Tendency
authors: Lan Zhao, Yuanyuan Ren, Naiwei Zou, Lin Li, Zhipeng Wu
abstract: To resolve decision-making conflicts between autonomous and human-driven vehicles in mixed traffic scenarios, this paper proposes an Interactive Decision-making Game Model with Dynamic Deduction (IDGM-DD). This method innovatively integrates short-term driving tendency prediction of other vehicles with incomplete-information dynamic game theory. Via the Weight Dynamic Inference (WDI) and Strategy Dynamic Adjustment (SDA) modules, it realizes real-time inference of interactive vehicles’ decision preferences and intelligent optimization of ego-vehicle strategies. Specifically, the WDI module uses Bayesian Inference to dynamically adjust payoff function weights based on real-time perception of the opponent’s driving tendency, while the SDA module establishes a response mechanism between ego-vehicle strategy execution intensity and the opponent’s tendency. Experiments on a multi-vehicle collaborative simulation platform show that the method outperforms static models significantly in efficiency (32% shorter decision-making time), payoff (45% improvement), and human-like driving similarity (86.03%). Further tests on the NGSIM dataset confirm a human-like similarity exceeding 93%. It effectively enhances the adaptability and safety of autonomous decision-making in complex scenarios, offering a novel theoretical framework and technical pathway for optimizing intelligent transportation systems.

title: Degradation-Resistant Infrared-Visible Image Fusion With Auto-Generated Textual Objectives and Embedded Contrastive Learning
authors: Yuhao Wang, Lingjuan Miao, Zhiqiang Zhou, Yajun Qiao, Yixuan Jiao
abstract: Infrared-visible image fusion aims to combine multi-modal image information to generate informative and robust scene representations, thereby enhancing perception capabilities and reliability in intelligent transportation systems. However, captured images often suffer from complex degradation issues, leading to low-quality source data. Existing methods are deficient in adapting to multiple degradation conditions, which limits their fusion performance. In this paper, we aim to develop a degradation-resistant image fusion method that automatically adapts to various degradations. For this purpose, we first construct an auto-generation prompt pipeline based on cascaded multi-modal and language models. It utilizes the vision-language understanding capabilities of large models to comprehensively detect degradation, then produces degradation prompts and corresponding text-based fusion objectives for each image. To resist degradations and produce the fusion results as described by fusion objectives, we next propose an embedded contrastive learning method within CLIP space to supervise the model training. This method ensures that the image fusion process is free from degradation and better aligned with the fusion objectives, which enhances the fusion model’s anti-degradation capability. Extensive experiments on public datasets validate the superiority and generalization ability of our method, and its robust degradation-adaptive capability makes it particularly suitable for complex scenes. The code is available at https://github.com/wyhlaowang/AutoFuse.

title: Hierarchical Event-Triggered Cooperative Control of Heterogeneous Vehicle Platoons Under Switching Topologies
authors: Zhiping Shen, Huarui Guo, Yilin Wu, Weikang Yang, Yonggui Liu
abstract: This paper studies the cooperative control problem for heterogeneous connected vehicle platoons (HCVPs) under switching topologies, which do not require each subgraph to be necessarily connected. First, to effectively save communication costs, a hierarchical control framework composed of an upper-level event-triggered observer (ETO) layer and a lower-level local tracking controller layer is proposed. Within the proposed framework, an ETO for each follower vehicle is designed to observe the leader, and a local tracking controller is designed using the proposed observer to ensure that each follower has the tracking capability of their own observer. Second, to improve the robustness of the system, a completely distributed control protocol is designed for jointly connected undirected topologies, which does not require global network information and is independent of switching rules. Meanwhile, to overcome the challenge of constructing Lyapunov function, a new convergence analysis method based on the contraction argument is employed for jointly connected directed topologies to solve the cooperative control problem of the vehicle platoon (VP). Third, the absence of Zeno-behavior in any finite time can be verified by showing that the event interval between any two consecutive triggering instants is strictly greater than zero. Finally, simulations are used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed protocols.

title: Probabilistic Modeling of Human Driver's Natural Behavior Distribution: An Ensemble Learning and GMM Framework for Car-Following Model
authors: Huihua Gao, Hong Chen, Ting Qu, Yongfu Li, Yunfeng Hu, Bingzhao Gao
abstract: Probabilistic modeling of the natural distribution of human driving behavior is crucial for constructing realistic and dynamic traffic simulation environments. To capture the complex, high-dimensional, and multi-modal characteristics of driving behavior, this paper proposes an ensemble-based probabilistic modeling framework. A Bayesian Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) is employed as a base predictor to model the multi-modal distribution, while ensemble learning is utilized to reduce model bias and improve robustness. To address challenges associated with high-dimensional features and limited sample sizes, dimensionality reduction and weighted bootstrap sampling are introduced to construct diverse meta models. An error evaluation network is developed to assess prediction quality in terms of mean, variance, and reliability. To handle distributional shifts across scenarios, an adaptive meta model with online learning capability is proposed for dynamic parameter updating and improved transferability. Furthermore, a reliability–uncertainty fusion strategy inspired by mean–variance theory is designed to dynamically assign optimal weights to individual meta models. Experiments on three datasets—HighD, SPMD, and MTBD—demonstrate superior performance in accuracy, robustness, and generalization.

title: ATSDAS: A Vision-Based System for Automated Traffic Sign Management and Condition Assessment
authors: Shucheng Zhang, Chenxi Liu, Nutvara Jantarathaneewat, Yinhai Wang
abstract: The maintenance and management of traffic signal assets are crucial for ensuring the safety and smooth operation of road transportation. However, timely repairs and updates of damaged traffic signs remain a significant challenge due to the inefficiency of manual measurements. This study proposes an innovative system that automates traffic sign collection and assessment using deep learning techniques. The system performs three key tasks, including traffic sign detection and tracking, condition assessment, and inventory building, by processing dashboard camera videos with GPS data or open-source street imagery. The system achieves a $\text {mAP}_{50}$ of 93.50% for detection and recognition and an accuracy of 93.56% for damage assessment by utilizing a retroreflectivity-related image feature extraction pipeline. The outputs are formalized into a visual inventory, enabling transportation agencies to manage traffic assets more efficiently. Field tests conducted in collaboration with the Washington State Department of Transportation validate the practical effectiveness of the framework. To further address the lack of publicly available condition datasets, this study also introduces the Damaged Traffic Sign Detection and Assessment (DTSDA) dataset, which combines real and synthetic images of damaged signs. Overall, the proposed approach offers a cost-effective and scalable alternative to the traditional labor-intensive method, thereby enhancing traffic asset management efficiency and contributing to safer transportation systems.

title: Taming Spatial Heterophily and Temporal Irregularity: A Curriculum Learning Approach for Traffic Forecasting
authors: Hongjun Wang, Zhiwen Zhang, Jiyuan Chen, Zipei Fan, Renhe Jiang, Wei Yuan, Ryosuke Shibasaki, Xuan Song
abstract: The advance in graph neural networks (GCNs) has propelled the development of spatial-temporal (ST) graph modeling (e.g., traffic flow prediction, and incident prediction) that intends to capture the inter-dependency between connected nodes and time sequence self-correlation simultaneously from dynamic node-level inputs. However, the existing literature trains their models with a random order, ignoring that the forecasting difficulty can vary significantly among node’s time sequences. Intuitively, the difficult samples indicate those patterns (e.g., abnormal patterns) are hard to learn by model directly. Thus, we consider that a curriculum with easy-to-difficult order, similar to the understanding procedure of humans, can improve the method’s performance in ST-graph modeling. Such an idea has a well-known name: curriculum learning (CL), which firstly designs the difficulty measurer for training samples and then feeds into the model with easy-to-difficult order according to the measurer. This paper explores the difficult time sequence whose temporal pattern is inconsistent with neighbors or has a poor auto-correlation. We design a spatial-temporal curriculum learning framework (STCL) trained by two additional ST tasks to obtain the vital power in ST imputation and measure each node’s signal difficulty corresponding to the performance in the auxiliary model in different ST scenarios. The ST-models are learned from scratch with explicit spatial affinities (subgraph) and easy temporal patterns, then progressively enrolled the nodes into the training dataset. Extensive experiments have been conducted in two public traffic flow datasets and two incident datasets, demonstrating our curriculum schedule’s superiority over without CL and other CL baselines.

title: UC-Track: Uncertainty-Aware and Task-Coupled 3-D Multi-Object Tracking
authors: Di Wu, Jiankun Peng, Shuangzhi Yu, Ke Xu, Zhijun Chen, Chunye Ma
abstract: Most existing multi-object tracking methods treat object detection, tracking, and prediction tasks separately, lacking collaborative optimization across tasks. This limitation hinders their ability to effectively handle environmental changes and perception uncertainty in real-world applications. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel end-to-end multi-task coupling framework, UC-Track (Uncertainty-aware and Task-coupled 3D Multi-Object Tracking). By integrating an uncertainty awareness mechanism and dynamic inter-task interaction strategy, UC-Track tightly couples object detection, tracking, and prediction tasks, thus enhancing tracking accuracy and system robustness in complex scenarios. First, an Uncertainty-aware Query Generation Module is introduced, which generates query vectors with uncertainty features based on object confidence scores. Second, a Refine 3D Box module is introduced to refine initial detections based on uncertainty-aware updated query states and historical query information, as part of the overall uncertainty-aware and task-coupled framework. Additionally, a trajectory prediction branch is employed to forecast the vehicle’s future trajectory, which, as coupled information, provides reference points for the next frame’s object detection and assists in target location estimation, especially under occlusion. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that UC-Track exhibits outstanding tracking accuracy on the nuScenes dataset, with an AMOTA of 0.438 and an AMOTP of 1.29, using input images with a shape of $800\times 320$ . Compared to the state-of-the-art PF-Track method, UC-Track achieves a significant improvement in overall tracking accuracy, particularly showing remarkable advantages when handling complex targets such as “trailer” and “bus”.

title: Bdes: Blockchain-Empowered Data and Energy Sharing in Internet of Electric Vehicles
authors: Xu Yang, Saiyu Qi, Wei Wei, Hongguang Zhao, Jingxian Cheng, Xinpei Dong, Qiuhao Wang, Ke Li, Wenjia Zhao
abstract: The Internet of Electric Vehicles (IoEV) facilitates intelligent and sustainable transportation by enabling electric vehicles (EVs) to participate in traffic data sharing and energy trading. However, the highly dynamic and decentralized nature of IoEV introduces critical challenges in identity authentication, data privacy, and trading security. Traditional centralized solutions are vulnerable to single points of failure and privacy leakage, while existing blockchain-based approaches often lack fine-grained identity control and unified handling of both data and energy interactions. To address these challenges, we propose Bdes, a blockchain-empowered data and energy sharing system tailored for IoEV environments. Bdes adopts a modular architecture that integrates three core components: a Decentralized Identifiers (DID) management module for decentralized identity registration and Verifiable Credential (VC) binding; a requirement matching module that enables automated, privacy-preserving authentication and matching between data and energy providers and consumers via smart contracts; and a trading module that decouples key exchange from data transmission, ensuring secure, tamper-proof, and traceable trading. By leveraging Decentralized Identifiers, Verifiable Credentials, and blockchain smart contracts, Bdes supports flexible, secure, and transparent sharing of traffic data and energy information across multiple untrusted entities. Extensive security analysis shows that Bdes effectively resists credential theft, inference attacks, and man-in-the-middle threats. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the system’s scalability, efficiency, and suitability for large-scale deployment in IoEV ecosystems.

title: MSCT: Addressing Time-Varying Confounding Bias With Marginal Structural Causal Transformer for Counterfactual Post-Crash Traffic Prediction
authors: Yansheng Liu, Shuang Li, Weiqi Li, Duxin Chen, Lu Dong, Nan Zhang, Daniel J. Graham, Pan Liu, Ziyuan Pu
abstract: Traffic crashes potentially lead to significant fatalities and injuries, in addition to causing major disruptions to traffic efficiency and substantial economic burdens. Accurate post-crash traffic prediction provides essential information for evaluating traffic perturbations and developing effective solutions for mitigating crash impacts. Previous studies have established a series of deep learning-based models to predict post-crash traffic conditions. Most of them were developed by learning statistical correlations among variables, however, time-varying confounder biases and the heterogeneous effects of crashes cannot be modeled by the correlation learning strategy. Especially for the post-crash prediction with hypothetical crash occurrence, the misunderstanding of the causal relationships among influential factors greatly hurts the effectiveness of the counterfactual prediction functions. By considering the aforementioned issues, the current study proposes the Marginal Structural Causal Transformer (MSCT), a novel causal deep learning model designed for counterfactual post-crash traffic prediction. To accommodate time-varying confounding biases, MSCT incorporates a structure inspired by Marginal Structural Models and introduces a balanced loss function to facilitate learning of invariant causal features. The proposed model is treatment-aware, which enables comprehending and predicting traffic speed under hypothetical crash intervention strategies. To validate the proposed MSCT, a synthetic data generation procedure is introduced to emulate the causal mechanisms between crashes and traffic dynamics. Extensive experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets for validating the proposed MSCT, including the prediction accuracy comparison under different degrees of time-varying confounding, varying crash ratios, consecutive crash scenarios, and ablation studies. The experimental results indicate that the proposed MSCT outperforms, for both factual and counterfactual predictions, not only non-causal deep learning models, e.g., Transformer and LLM, but also the cutting-edge causal deep learning methods. Notably, MSCT maintains robust performance even under complex scenarios such as multi-crash conditions. The research findings demonstrate the effectiveness of MSCT for assessing hypothetical crash scenarios and supporting proactive traffic management. Future research directions include spatial causal model development and exploring broader applications across various transportation systems.

title: STCNet: SVO-Guided Two-Stage Clustering Network for Driving Style Recognition
authors: Jianwen Zhang, Wensheng Luo, Guanghui Sun, Xiaoxu Peng, Dong Zhou
abstract: The classification of driving styles is of paramount importance in intelligent transportation systems (ITS) owing to its potential to improve driving safety, optimize driving comfort, and mitigate energy consumption. This paper introduces STCNet, an SVO-guided two-stage clustering network for driving style recognition, consisting of two main components: the representation module and the clustering module. Specifically, the representation module employs a long short-term memory (LSTM)-based autoencoder to derive a low-dimensional representation containing the driving behavior characteristics of both lateral and longitudinal driving data. The clustering module is divided into two stages: first, the fuzzy C-means clustering method is applied to estimate the membership of aggressive and conservative driving styles for initial rough clustering. Then, a social value orientation (SVO)-guided clustering is introduced to refine the clustering process and enhance the interpretability. Through a two-stage training process: pretraining the representation module and then jointly training these two modules, a high-quality and clustering-friendly representation is extracted, thereby improving clustering performance. The Next Generation Simulation (NGSIM) public dataset is leveraged to train and evaluate our approach, demonstrating its effectiveness in driving style recognition.

title: A Terrain-Interactive Autonomous Switching Control Strategy for the Land-Air Bimodal Robot
authors: Song Yang, Wenshuai Yu, Shoubin Chen, Fei Ma, Zhou Liu, Qingquan Li
abstract: In recent years, land-air bimodal robots, which leverage the extended endurance of wheeled robots and the maneuverability of quadrotor robots, have garnered significant attention. This paper addresses the challenges of motion control and autonomous mode-switching in land-air bimodal robots navigating sloping terrains with unknown slope angles and varying surface materials. Firstly, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the robot’s dynamics models in both modes, representing them as a uniform second-order nonlinear state-space formulation incorporating unknown uncertainties. This uniformly represented formulation is beneficial to controller design for two modes and facilitates the deployment of the bimodal controller in a low-cost microcontroller. Then, a terrain-aware controller is proposed for land mode without the accurate dynamics models, and it can overcome the influence of unknown uncertainties brought by unstructured sloping terrains. Subsequently, in order to improve the robot’s endurance, an autonomous mode-switching control strategy is explored for maximizing the use of wheeled land mode to cross sloping terrains. Finally, we conduct the first real-world experiment with a self-developed land-air robot in some sloping terrains with different slope angles and surface materials to validate the accessibility in three-dimensional space of the land-air bimodal robot with the proposed switching control strategy.

title: Adaptive Control of Heterogeneous Platoons With Guaranteed Collision Avoidance
authors: Ashutosh Chandra Pandey, Sayan Basu Roy, Simone Baldi
abstract: This work proposes a guaranteed collision avoidance framework for Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control of a vehicular platoon characterized by unidirectional communication and heterogeneous parameters. In the proposed framework, the actual (heterogeneous) platoon is made to converge to a reference (homogeneous) platoon via adaptive laws designed using of set-theoretic model reference adaptive control. Yet, in contrast to the state-of-art that is based on ensuring collision avoidance on the reference platoon dynamics only, the approach we propose can ensure collision avoidance on the actual platoon dynamics. This result is possible thanks to the introduction of a novel concept of virtual platoon, only used for analysis, but that does not interact with the actual platoon. The stability and convergence properties of the proposed framework are established using Lyapunov-based analysis in conjunction with the aforementioned virtual platoon concept. Simulation results further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Structural Feature Modulation for Day--Night Cross-Domain Object Re-Identification
authors: Simin Zhan, Yifan Shi, Pudu Liu, Liu Liu, Jianqing Zhu, Huanqiang Zeng, Zhen Lei
abstract: Day-night cross-domain object re-identification presents significant challenges due to severe illumination-induced domain gaps. Unlike conventional attention mechanisms that suffer from limited dimensional coverage and rely on single-type normalization strategies, we propose a structural feature modulation (SFM) approach that operates from a modulation perspective. Our SFM approach incorporates a gated batch-layer normalization strategy within the modulation architecture, resulting in the construction of a gated normalization-based modulation (GNM) module. This module effectively leverages the complementary advantages of both batch normalization and layer normalization to balance intra-domain discriminability and cross-domain generalization. Furthermore, we develop a multi-granularity modulation (MGM) module that recalibrates features across both edge-granularity and area-granularity pathways, enabling comprehensive structural modulation. Extensive experiments on the DN-348 and LLCM benchmark datasets demonstrate that our SFM approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, achieving notable improvements including a 2.51% mAP increase on the DN-348 dataset. Our codes are available at https://github.com/SimiiZ/SFM

title: An Intention-Driven Lane Change Framework Considering Heterogeneous Dynamic Cooperation in Mixed-Traffic Environments
authors: Xiaoyun Qiu, Haichao Liu, Yue Pan, Jun Ma, Xinhu Zheng
abstract: In mixed-traffic environments, autonomous vehicles (AVs) must interact with heterogeneous human-driven vehicles (HVs) whose intentions and driving styles vary across individuals and scenarios. Such variability introduces uncertainty into lane change interactions, where safety and efficiency critically depend on accurately anticipating surrounding drivers'cooperative responses. Existing methods often oversimplify these interactions by assuming uniform or fixed behavioral patterns. To address this limitation, we propose an intention-driven lane change framework that integrates driving-style recognition with cooperation-aware decision-making and motion-planning. A deep learning-based classifier identifies distinct human driving styles in real time. We then introduce a dual-perspective cooperation score composed of intrinsic style-dependent tendencies and interactive dynamic components, enabling interpretable and adaptive intention prediction and quantitative inference. A decision-making module combines behavior cloning (BC) and inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) to determine lane change feasibility. Later, a coordinated motion-planning architecture integrating IRL-based intention inference with model predictive control (MPC) is established to generate collision-free and socially compliant trajectories. Experiments on the NGSIM dataset show that the proposed decision-making model outperforms representative rule-based and learning-based baselines, achieving 96.98% accuracy in lane change classification. Motion-planning evaluations further demonstrate improved maneuver success and execution stability in mixed-traffic environments. These results validate the effectiveness of structured cooperation modeling for intention-driven autonomous lane changes.

title: LLM-ODDR: A Large Language Model Framework for Joint Order Dispatching and Driver Repositioning
authors: Tengfei Lyu, Siyuan Feng, Hao Liu, Hai Yang
abstract: Ride-hailing platforms face significant challenges in optimizing order dispatching and driver repositioning operations in dynamic urban environments. Traditional approaches based on combinatorial optimization, rule-based heuristics, and reinforcement learning often overlook driver income fairness, interpretability, and adaptability to real-world dynamics. To address these gaps, we propose LLM-ODDR, a novel framework leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) for joint Order Dispatching and Driver Repositioning (ODDR) in ride-hailing services. LLM-ODDR framework comprises three key components: (1) Multi-objective-guided Order Value Refinement, which evaluates orders by considering multiple objectives to determine their overall value; (2) Fairness-aware Order Dispatching, which balances platform revenue with driver income fairness; and (3) Spatiotemporal Demand-Aware Driver Repositioning, which optimizes idle vehicle placement based on historical patterns and projected supply. We also develop JointDR-GPT, a fine-tuned model optimized for ODDR tasks with domain knowledge. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets from Manhattan taxi operations demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms traditional methods in terms of effectiveness, adaptability to anomalous conditions, and decision interpretability. To our knowledge, this is the first exploration of LLMs as decision-making agents in ride-hailing ODDR tasks, establishing foundational insights for integrating advanced language models within intelligent transportation systems. While the current framework incurs higher computational costs than traditional methods, we show that parallel decomposition and model distillation can reduce latency to production-viable levels for deployment.

title: Cluster Fault-Tolerant Consensus Control for Heterogeneous Unmanned Systems With Prescribed Performance
authors: Mengna Li, Ziquan Yu
abstract: The coordination of air-sea heterogeneous unmanned systems (HUSs) can significantly improve the transportation efficiency of maritime transportation systems. However, various faults can affect the control performance and coordination of HUSs, leading to a decrease in the safety and reliability of maritime transportation. Therefore, this paper focuses on the problem of cluster fault-tolerant consensus control (FTCC) with prescribed performance for HUSs consisting of a group of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) under actuator faults. Firstly, based on pinning control and an error transformation with singularity avoidance, a distributed state estimator with prescribed performance is designed to estimate the output of the cluster leaders, and ensure that the estimation error converges to the predefined range within a prescribed time. Then, lumped fault term in HUSs is compensated by neural networks (NNs), and a new type of updating law for NN weights is designed by the immersion and invariance (I&I) adaptive theory. Finally, by using this error transformation and dynamic surface control, a cluster FTCC law with preset precision and prescribed time is proposed to achieve prescribed performance cluster consensus of HUSs under actuator faults. Lyapunov analysis proves that the formation error of HUSs can converge to the specified range within a prescribed time. Simulation test and comparative analysis verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: RIDE: Boosting 3-D Object Detection for LiDAR Point Clouds via Rotation-Invariant Analysis
authors: Zhaoxuan Wang, Xu Han, Hongxin Liu, Xianzhi Li
abstract: The rotation robustness property has drawn much attention to point cloud analysis, whereas it still poses a critical challenge in 3D object detection. When subjected to arbitrary rotation, most existing detectors fail to produce expected outputs due to the poor rotation robustness. In this paper, we present RIDE, a pioneering exploration of Rotation-Invariance for the 3D LiDAR-point-based object DEtector, with the key idea of designing rotation-invariant features from LiDAR scenes and then effectively incorporating them into existing 3D detectors. Specifically, we design a bi-feature extractor that extracts 1) object-aware features that are sensitive to rotation but preserve geometry well, and 2) rotation-invariant features, which lose geometric information to a certain extent but are robust to rotation. These two kinds of features complement each other to decode 3D proposals that are robust to arbitrary rotations. Particularly, our RIDE is compatible and easy to plug into the existing one-stage and two-stage 3D detectors, and boosts both detection performance and rotation robustness. Extensive experiments on the standard benchmarks showcase that the mean average precision (mAP) and rotation robustness can be significantly boosted by integrating with our RIDE, with +5.6% mAP and 111% rotation robustness improvement on KITTI, +5.1% and 34% improvement correspondingly on nuScenes. The code is available at https://github.com/CentauriStar/RIDE

title: CPCoCo: Localization-Free Collaborative Perception via Attentive Contrastive Consensus
authors: Langkun Xu, Chenyang Li, Zhongxiang Zhao, Lin Wang
abstract: Collaborative perception compensates for the limitations of individual agents by facilitating information exchange among multiple agents, with relative pose transformations serving as the foundation for effective collaboration. Current collaborative perception systems rely heavily on precise localization information for relative pose transformations, but achieving robust localization in real-world scenarios remains a significant challenge. To overcome this, we introduce CPCoCo, a robust collaborative perception framework that eliminates the need for external localization. Specifically, we propose a feature-based attention contrastive learning module. It utilizes an attention mechanism to identify similar structures within features, thereby resolving cross-view feature inconsistencies. Concurrently, it employs a consistency consensus mechanism to filter for more reliable feature matching, ultimately achieving the alignment of multi-agent coordinate systems. The proposed approach can be seamlessly integrated into existing multi-agent collaborative object detection frameworks for end-to-end training. Extensive experiments on both real-world and simulated datasets demonstrate that CPCoCo achieves state-of-the-art detection performance in localization-free settings, with an average processing time of approximately 18 ms. Code is available on https://github.com/saki-mobile/cpcoco

title: Detecting Black Hole and Volcano Tidal Patterns in Free-Floating Bike-Sharing Systems: Balancing Computational Efficiency and Accuracy
authors: Wendong Chen, Jiemin Kang, Long Cheng, Mengqiu Cao, Lan Wu
abstract: In the case of free-floating bike-sharing (FFBS) systems, it is essential to be able to detect ‘black holes’, characterised by substantial flow convergence, and ‘volcanoes’, marked by pronounced flow divergence, in order to understand supply-demand imbalances driven by tidal patterns. However, the Modifiable Areal Unit Problem (MAUP) limits the effectiveness of traditional detection methods based on aggregated units such as grids or traffic analysis zones. To overcome this issue, we propose a road-segment-based, two-stage framework that integrates management subzone delineation with tidal pattern detection, thus balancing computational efficiency and identification accuracy. Using Nanjing, China, as a case study, we detect tidal patterns across holidays, weekdays, and weekends. The results show that black holes and volcanoes cluster in midday off-peak and evening peaks during holidays, dominate in the morning and evening peaks on weekdays, and are distributed more evenly across weekends. Land-use analysis indicates that weekday black holes are concentrated around metro stations and employment districts during morning peaks, and around metro stations and residential districts during evening peaks. This reflects the widespread use of FFBS for ‘first/last-mile’ connections between homes or workplaces and metro stations, causing concentrated bike accumulation. Geometric properties further reveal that tidal patterns at the road-segment level exhibit irregular shapes and multi-scale characteristics, which conventional aggregated units fail to capture due to the MAUP. These findings help to improve understanding of FFBS supply-demand interactions and provide detailed policy recommendations for designing targeted FFBS operational strategies to enhance efficiency and service quality.

title: Energy-Based Adaptive Cruise Control With Structurally Induced Self-Excited Driving for Car-Following
authors: Yuntae Kim, Byungjun Kim, Dasol Jeong, Hyuck-Kee Lee, Seibum B. Choi
abstract: This paper proposes a novel energy-based adaptive cruise control (ACC) algorithm for car-following that fundamentally redefines the control target. Conventional ACC, formulated as a spacing-error regulation problem, structurally leads to frequent actuator switching under realistic driving conditions, which can increase control effort and limit opportunities for fuel-efficient behavior. To address these limitations, the proposed controller regulates a desired energy level within the car-following system instead of minimizing tracking errors with respect to the preceding vehicle. This change induces structurally self-excited driving, forming a loop in the relative distance–velocity domain and enabling Pulse-and-Glide-like behavior without relying on rule-based switching or gain tuning. To ensure safety during self-excited driving, a tube-based control structure is introduced, within which the system remains bounded. Additionally, a parameter update mechanism is incorporated to further reduce the influence of the preceding vehicle. Together, these features enable smoother control inputs, improved road load utilization, and reduced control effort from the lower-level controller. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms conventional ACC and production-level Smart Cruise Control (SCC) systems in terms of control smoothness and energy efficiency, while maintaining a safe following distance. The algorithm also satisfies string stability, validating its applicability in multi-vehicle scenarios. Overall, the proposed approach offers a structurally interpretable and driver-personalizable framework for efficient and robust car-following.

title: TEg-STGNN: Learning Time-Evolving Heterogeneity in Spatial-Temporal Traffic Networks
authors: Lutao Zheng, Guanjun Liu, Ying Tang
abstract: Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Networks (STGNNs) have become a dominant paradigm for traffic modeling due to their ability to capture spatial and temporal dependencies in traffic networks. However, existing methods typically rely on a uniform representation for modeling temporal dependencies, which fails to capture the evolutionary heterogeneity of traffic dynamics under varying scenarios. Consequently, despite achieving competitive overall results, their performance is often compromised in critical scenarios. Specifically, traffic dynamics under different scenarios manifest as heterogeneous temporal patterns, which are generally categorized into short-term fluctuations with quick dissipation and long-term trends that evolve gradually. Effectively representing these temporal patterns while mitigating their interference is crucial for enhancing model generalization across diverse scenarios. To bridge this gap, we propose a Time-Evolving Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Network (TEg-STGNN), a novel framework that incorporates the time-evolving heterogeneity of traffic dynamics. Our approach introduces a dynamic graph construction module that encodes scenario-specific patterns, along with a dual-pathway architecture designed to disentangle short-term disturbances from long-term evolutionary trends. A learnable gating network dynamically fuses these disentangled representations, ensuring robust prediction performance across diverse traffic scenarios. Comprehensive experiments on real-world datasets show that TEg-STGNN excels in predicting specific congestion scenarios and maintains strong generalization across a wide range of traffic conditions.

title: Sketching the Dynamics of Traffic: Data-Efficient Predictive Connected Cruise Control
authors: Minghao Shen, Jeff Scruggs, Gabor Orosz
abstract: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication enables connected cruise control by providing upstream traffic information beyond the line of sight. However, practical V2X deployments face challenges including packet loss, limited training data, and domain shifts between different driving conditions. In this paper, we propose a data-driven prediction framework that addresses these challenges through memory-efficient online adaptation. The ego vehicle predicts the speed of the vehicle immediately ahead based on the speeds of connected vehicles in the upstream traffic. We derive an input-output model from state-space car-following dynamics and develop a Gaussian sketching algorithm that enables efficient online adaptation, reducing per-step update complexity and memory compared to the full-dimension recursive least squares (RLS) algorithm. We validate the framework using real-world traffic data under challenging scenarios: cross-domain transfer, limited warmstart data, and V2X packet loss. The proposed Gaussian sketch method achieves a 34.4% improvement under input distribution shift, outperforming both non-adaptive and full RLS baselines. It also reaches up to 92.1% improvement with limited warmstart data. Crucially, the method maintains a 30.7% improvement even under 50% packet loss, demonstrating robustness to realistic V2X communication impairments.

title: Modeling Paradigms for Adaptive Decentralized Traffic Control via a Rollout Reinforcement Learning Approach
authors: Zhongyang Lu, Andy H. F. Chow, Zicheng Su, Wanjing Ma
abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic modeling framework that integrates rollout reinforcement learning (RL) with tractable traffic models for adaptive decentralized traffic control. The traffic control problem is represented as a Markov decision process, aiming to minimize network delay under stochastic traffic demand through acyclic signal plans. To address the instability issue of model-free RL methods, we incorporate a model-based rollout component into the RL optimization framework, where the point queue and spatial queue models are adopted to explicitly represent network flow propagation. This approach enables more reliable estimations of traffic states and system costs through model-based rollout simulations derived from real data within the planning horizon. Fed with the rollout traffic states, a state-dependent surrogate function is proposed to parameterize the unknown optimal value function, which significantly mitigates the curse of dimensionality when recursively calculating the Bellman equation. A multi-step temporal difference learning method is employed to train the neural network-based surrogate function with realized transitions collected from the external environment, enhancing the accuracy of the value function approximation while correcting model-plant mismatch. Additionally, the framework adopts a decentralized architecture, enabling asynchronous operation across intersections that reduces computational burden while maintaining network-level coordination. Validation on three urban networks demonstrates that the proposed controllers can effectively mitigate delays and queue spillback even in oversaturated scenarios. Notably, the point queue model achieves performance comparable to the spatial queue model with high precision, highlighting that the proposed framework is generic across different traffic models even without sophisticated calibration and complex propagation laws.

title: Image Segmentation With Large Language Models: A Survey With Perspectives for Intelligent Transportation Systems
authors: Sanjeda Akter, Ibne Farabi Shihab, Anuj Sharma
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) with computer vision is profoundly transforming perception tasks like image segmentation. For intelligent transportation systems (ITS), where accurate scene understanding is critical for safety and efficiency, this new paradigm offers unprecedented capabilities. This survey systematically reviews the emerging field of LLM-augmented image segmentation, focusing on its applications, challenges, and future directions within ITS.
