title: Tracking Large-Scale Shared Bikes With Inertial Motion Learning in GNSS Blocked Environments
authors: Feng Liu, Kejia Li, Zhiwei Yang, Chunwei Yang, Qun Li, Guobin Wu, Qiang Ni, Ruipeng Gao
abstract: Although Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) provide a general solution for bike tracking outdoors, there still exist complex riding environments where only inertial navigation systems work, such as urban canyons. Despite decades of research, localization using only low-cost inertial sensors still faces challenges such as cumulative drifts and poor robustness caused by filtering methods. Furthermore, sensors such as visual and LiDAR could provide reliable measurements, but they are not suitable for large-scale deployment. In this paper, we propose an inertial tracking framework that integrates bicycle mechanical constraints with a mixture-of-experts model. Specifically, we leverage multiple expert modules to capture shared representations and weight them through the gating mechanism, thus improving multi-task learning performance and enabling uncertainty-aware trajectory estimation. Furthermore, based on the mechanical transmission between the pedal and the rear wheel of a bike, we explore the intrinsic relationship between the rider's periodic pedalling behaviors and acceleration variations, and convert such patterns into bike's wheel speed for dynamic calibration. Experiments with real-world riding data from shared bikes of the DiDi ride-hailing platform demonstrate that our system improves the accuracy of baselines by at least 12%, with wheel speed errors below 0.5 m/s at 95-percentile.

title: GeoLogistics Transformer: Exploring Urban Truck Traffic With Route-Adaptive Embedding and Contextual Logistics Graph
authors: Gen Li, Jishi Wu, Zhongwei Luo, Tao Feng, Zongyuan Wu
abstract: Accurate prediction of urban truck traffic is essential for efficient logistics and traffic management but remains challenging due to complex spatiotemporal dynamics. This study proposes the GeoLogistics Transformer (GLT), a forecasting model that integrates mobility patterns of different truck types, geographic context, and logistics attributes. Using truck trajectory data from Tokyo, GLT combines graph-based learning, temporal encoding, and Transformer-based spatial attention over grid tokens to capture both long-range logistics and temporal dependencies. Experimental results show that GLT achieves the highest explained variance at the immediate forecast horizon and consistently matches or outperforms benchmark models in mean absolute error (MAE) across longer horizons. The results highlight the importance of logistics-aware spatial modeling and truck type specific representations for urban truck traffic prediction.

title: Predefined Time Cooperative Control Strategy for Multi-Vectored Water-Jet Robots Transport Using Unknown Payload Dynamics
authors: Lei Wang, Huiming Xing, Yong Gao, Chunying Li, Shuxiang Guo, Guangchun Li
abstract: To address these cooperative transport challenges of multiple underwater robot systems (MURs) in densely cluttered underwater environments, such as model uncertainties, external disturbances, and unknown payload dynamics, this paper proposes a predefined time cooperative transport strategy. First, a payload centered local gradient based trajectory generation method for traversing narrow passages. Second, we develop a predefined time disturbance observer (PTDO) to estimate the disturbances, and payload forces. The PTDO provides feedback to the controller while ensuring that the estimation error converges to a bounded value within a predefined time. Finally, a predefined time backstepping based tracking controller (PTC) is developed such that the tracking errors enter a prescribed residual set within a user assigned time bound, and this bound is independent of the initial conditions. The Lyapunov stability theory and simulation results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed strategy in cooperative payload transport tasks.

title: Dual-Mode SPL-SLAM: A Robust Semantic Point-Line SLAM System With Monocular Neural Depth and Sensor Fusion for Intelligent Transportation
authors: Zhen Tian, Zhihao Lin, Dezong Zhao, Christos Anagnostopoulos, Peng Wang, Wenjing Zhao, Lin Wu, Qi Zhang
abstract: —Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is critical for Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), yet existing solutions struggle to balance accuracy, sensor versatility, and computational efficiency. Traditional monocular methods suffer from scale drift, while RGB-D systems with heavy semantic networks often exceed the computational budgets of onboard processors. To address these conflicting constraints, we propose Dual-Mode SPL-SLAM, a unified adaptive framework capable of adapting to different intelligent driving agents. The system intel-ligently switches between two operating paths: Mode I (Sensor-Semantic) leverages physical depth sensors and high-precision semantic segmentation for complex dynamic environments. To further improve accuracy, we use line-feature processing and a refined epipolar-constraint error for robust detection of known and unknown dynamic objects; Mode II (Neural-Clustering) employs a lightweight neural network (LiteMono) and K-means++ clustering within the object bounding box predicted by GPU-accelerated YOLOX to recover scale and filter dynamic objects using fast LK optical flow in monocular setups. Crucially, both modes converge into a shared Adaptive Point-Line Backend, which dynamically weights features based on environmental texture to ensure robustness. Extensive experiments on KITTI dataset demonstrate that our system achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and real-time performance across diverse sensor configurations.

title: Multi-Modal Trajectory Prediction With Frenet Trajectory Translation
authors: Boqi Li, Shaobing Xu, Huei Peng
abstract: This paper presents a trajectory prediction algorithm called Frenet Trajectory Translation, which predicts future trajectories in the Frenet coordinate system conditioned on vehicle interactions, maps, and routes, all represented as graphs. Our method can accurately predict future motions by identifying distinct modalities derived from various routes and maneuvers. Additionally, since the predictions occur in the Frenet coordinate system, they inherently support multi-modality, allowing for generating counterfactual future trajectories based on diverse routing intentions. Additionally, we propose a novel modality sampling method to enhance the diversity of future motions and thus offer better modality coverage. Our algorithm has been tested across different roundabout locations, delivering state-of-the-art results. We conclude by integrating the Frenet Trajectory Translation with a downstream trajectory planner, showcasing combined prediction and planning outcomes in a simulated environment. The source code is available at https://github.com/studybox/FTT

title: A Tutorial on Future Vehicular Communications: From Performance Metrics to Open Research Directions
authors: Junliang Ye, Xiaohu Ge, Yuxi Zhao, Yue Yu, Hamid Gharavi
abstract: The study of vehicular networks has evolved into a new era thanks to rapid advances in electric, transportation, communication, and automobile technologies. However, the realization of modern applications like autonomous driving, intelligent transportation systems, and the smart city remain a major challenge due to the high requirements for performance metrics like data rate, latency, reliability, connectivity, coverage, and security. Moreover, in vehicular network, the performance metrics are not independent and may have a complex coupling relationship, i.e., optimizing one may result in degrading others. In this paper, we begin with discussing the coupling effect among the aforementioned performance metrics, aiming to provide a basic concept of the challenges of future vehicular networks. We aim to provide a comprehensive review of recent developments in vehicular communication technologies, such as the fifth-generation new radio (5G NR), dedicated short-range communications (DSRC), millimeter wave/terahertz communications, mobile edge computing (MEC), integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted vehicular networks, and blockchain-assisted security. The paper also covers the role of AI and its impact on the performance of each of the aforementioned applications. We then summarize several promising areas that can influence the future research in vehicular networks. Lastly, the paper concludes by highlighting key research challenges and future directions in the domain of vehicular networks.

title: Optimizing Nursing Care Taxi Dispatch Leveraging Integer Linear Programming Solvers and Machine Learning
authors: Riku Nakao, Akihito Hiromori, Hamada Rizk, Hirozumi Yamaguchi
abstract: In this paper, we formulate a new vehicle dispatch optimization problem, called Nursing Care Taxi Dispatch, as a variant of the Vehicle Routing Problem, considering constraints related to wheelchair use, user compatibility, pick-up and drop-off times, and vehicle limitations. Previous neural-based methods for Vehicle Routing Problems have typically addressed a few simple constraints, while our new problem involves multiple complex constraints, resulting in having fewer destinations to select. This complexity makes it more difficult to obtain solutions that allow all nodes to be visited with a limited number of vehicles. To balance low violation rate, computational efficiency, and solution quality, we propose a supervised machine learning approach based on the Transformer architecture. We first obtain a set of high-quality solutions using an integer linear programming solver for given inputs and then train our learning model through supervised learning. Additionally, we introduce the post-processing of the paths generated by the learning model, ensuring that all constraints are satisfied. We compared each instance's objective function value (operating time), execution time, and constraint violation rate across different methods: our proposed method and some existing methods including integer linear programming and machine learning-based methods, using real-world facility data. Our method successfully produced balanced solutions regarding operating time, execution time, and constraint violation rate. Notably, we observed a decrease in the operating time for all problem sizes and regions, while keeping constraint violations to a minimum compared to existing methods. Especially, the decrease reached up to 8% for problem sizes with fewer than 30 users.

title: StructFormer: A Transformer-Based Multi-Structure Attention Model for Solving Routing Problems
authors: Longze Liu, Peilan He, Yanwei Yu, Guiyuan Jiang, Yidan Sun, Junyu Dong, Muwei Jian, Siew-Kei Lam
abstract: Vehicle Routing Problems (VRPs), fundamental NP-hard challenges in intelligent transportation systems, often pose scalability challenges and require expert-dependent design when solved with traditional heuristics. Neural VRP solvers offer data-driven alternatives but suffer from limitations such as the “averaging effect” in self-attention, which impairs key-node differentiation and the modeling of salient structural relationships. Existing feature enhancement methods also overlook key structural patterns, limiting representation quality. To address these challenges, we propose StructFormer, a transformer-based improvement solver with multiview structural attention. Its core Multi-StructAttn module integrates multiview structural embeddings to mitigate the averaging effect, enhancing node differentiation and capturing salient structural relationships. Additionally, a global-centrality-based feature enhancement module embeds optimal connection patterns, enriching structural representation. A novel decoder further incorporates search-state-dependent dynamic heuristic information to improve step-wise decision-making during iterative refinement. Experiments on diverse TSP and CVRP benchmarks demonstrate that StructFormer consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models. Furthermore, some modules of StructFormer are compatible with other learning-based solvers, offering significant performance gains on both TSP and CVRP.

title: GPT-EV: Generative Pre-Training for Charging Demand Prediction of Electric Vehicle
authors: Tianjing Wang, Sheng Zhong, Shuqi Xie, Houbo Xiong, Zhao Yang Dong
abstract: While various machine learning techniques have been applied to charging demand prediction of electric vehicle (EV), existing methods lack a dedicated generative pre-training method capable of effectively capturing spatio-temporal dependencies in EV charging behaviors. This limitation hampers their generalization ability and prediction accuracy across diverse regions and time scales. To address this issue, this study proposes GPT-EV, a generative pre-training (GPT) method specifically designed for EV charging demand prediction. GPT-EV integrates an adaptive attention masking strategy to enhance the extraction of key temporal patterns, a customized spatio-temporal encoding mechanism to model intricate spatial-temporal relationships, and a decoder with probabilistic generation to improve robustness against uncertainties in charging behavior. These advancements enable the model to learn transferable representations, ensuring high-accuracy predictions across different regions and time scales even with minimal fine-tuning data. Experimental evaluations confirm that GPT-EV surpasses conventional deep learning and time-series GPT models across diverse regions and forecasting horizons, highlighting its potential to enhance mobility-aware energy management and integrated transportation-power planning.

title: Game-Based Target Enclosing Control of Autonomous Surface Vehicles Against Actuator Faults
authors: Hongye Zhang, Yong Chen
abstract: Autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs), as vital vehicles in port traffic management, necessitate robust control research for their complex operations. This article investigates the target enclosing control of ASVs suffering from actuator faults and environment disturbances, with a focus on ensuring reliable traffic monitoring tasks. Fault tolerant control (FTC) based on a two-level differential game is proposed to encircle the target. First, the cooperative target enclosing problems of ASVs with actuator faults are proposed and auxiliary control laws are developed to achieve the maritime traffic monitoring tasks. Unlike the traditional kinetic controller design method, the two-level games are established in this paper to design the controllers. On the one hand, the total disturbances consisting of actuator faults and environmental disturbances is considered as one player, constituting a zero-sum differential game with the kinetic controller. On the other hand, based on the topology graph, the whole ASV system constructs a graphical game, in which each vehicle is a player to find the control policies achieving the global Nash equilibrium (GNE). Moreover, the two-level game problem is solved by adaptive dynamic programming, which leads to the distributed kinetic FTC laws. The control policies enable the target enclosing task, the fault-tolerant task and the Nash equilibrium (NE) task. Finally, the result analysis proves the effectiveness of the algorithm.

title: Adaptive Neural Event-Triggered Control of Vehicular Platoons With Input Saturation Constraint and Unknown Disturbances
authors: Yan-Jun Liu, Jiahui Wei, Hao Chen, Lei Liu
abstract: This article studies the problem of robust adaptive event-triggered control for connected vehicular platoon systems with input saturation constraint and unknown disturbances. First, the approximation identity of neural network is utilized to solve the unknown nonlinear functions. Then, based on constant time headway, the position tracking error and coupled sliding surface are constructed. Under backstepping recursion, the Lyapunov function is selected to develop auxiliary control functions. The adaptive event-triggered mechanism is developed to compensate for saturation effects through auxiliary control functions. The proposed control theory can reduce unnecessary transmission of communication resources and assure boundedness of the closed-loop system for all involved signals. And it guarantees that the Zeno behavior is eliminated. Finally, the feasibility of the presented method is justified with the simulation results.

title: From Camera-Based Sensing to Reasoning: A Comprehensive Review Toward Proactive Vulnerable Road User Safety
authors: Shucheng Zhang, Yan Shi, Bingzhang Wang, Yuang Zhang, Muhammad Monjurul Karim, Kehua Chen, Chenxi Liu, Mehrdad Nasri, Yinhai Wang
abstract: Ensuring the safety of vulnerable road users (VRUs), such as pedestrians and cyclists, remains a critical challenge, as conventional infrastructure-based measures are often insufficient in dynamic urban environments. Recent advances in learning-based visual sensing systems have created new opportunities for more adaptive and context-aware VRU protection. This paper presents a comprehensive review of camera-based methods for proactive VRU safety, with a focus on developments over the past five years. Unlike prior surveys that primarily emphasize detection, we organize the literature into three interconnected components: visual perception (detection and classification), motion modeling (tracking and trajectory prediction), and behavior understanding (intent recognition and reasoning). These components form a unified hierarchical pipeline that enables early risk anticipation and timely intervention. Furthermore, this survey systematically incorporates emerging AI paradigms, including Vision Transformers (ViTs), Large Language Models (LLMs), and diffusion models, highlighting their roles in representation learning, uncertainty modeling, and semantic reasoning. Finally, we identify four key challenges specific to VRU safety, including data scarcity, behavioral uncertainty, edge deployment efficiency, and real-world sensing constraints, and discuss corresponding research directions. This work provides a unified foundation for the development of reliable, scalable, and deployable VRU safety systems.

title: 3-bit Transmission Mechanism-Based Adaptive Neural Path Following Control of 4DOF Underactuated USVs via Error-Constraint ILOS Approach
authors: Guibing Zhu, Junhui Li, Yong Ma, Zhixiong Li, M. Sotelo
abstract: This paper investigates the path-following control problem for 4-degree-of-freedom (4DOF) underactuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) under internal/external uncertainties. The proposed control framework comprises the guidance and control modules. For the guidance subsystem, a novel error-constraint integral line-of-sight (EC-ILOS) method is originally developed to resolve the underactuation challenge. In the control subsystem, a virtual parameter learning-based adaptive neural network technique is proposed to counteract uncertainty impacts. To lighten the burden of data transmission in controller-actuator (C-A) channels, an innovative 3-bit transmission mechanism is designed, featuring a specialized encoder-decoder pair with a novel encoding strategy. The developed 3-bit transmission mechanism-based EC-ILOS adaptive neural control solution is endowed with two key advantages: 1) It achieves user-defined performance while eliminating parameter tuning difficulties in guidance systems; 2) It significantly reduces C-A channel data transmission through the new encoder-decoder mechanism. The Lyapunov stability theorem is used to analyze the convergence of all closed-loop system signals. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

title: Robust Lateral Control of a Convoy of Autonomous and Connected Vehicles With Limited Preview
authors: Mengke Liu, Neelkamal Somisetty, Sivakumar Rathinam, Swaroop Darbha
abstract: This paper investigates the lateral control of Connected and Autonomous Vehicle (CAV) convoys during lane change (LC) maneuvers in general and emergency lane change (ELC) maneuvers in particular. ELC maneuvers are initiated in response to emergency cues from either the front or rear of the convoy, enabling obstacle avoidance or facilitating the movement of other vehicles. The primary objective is to develop a lateral control strategy for CAVs leveraging inter-vehicular communication while not relying on position information from the road. This is particularly useful for lateral control of convoys when the road information is not readily available. A key assumption is the reliable connectivity among CAVs, allowing each vehicle to access GPS position traces from both the leading and immediate predecessor vehicles. This connectivity enables the construction of a composite LC trajectory, serving as a discretized preview of the desired trajectory. The proposed methodology entails trajectory construction, computation of cross-track, heading, and yaw-rate errors, and the formulation of a lateral control law. Furthermore, this paper assesses the robustness of the controller under varying longitudinal velocities and examines lateral string instability when lead-vehicle information is unavailable. Numerical results from sensitivity analyses and robustness tests demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed lateral control scheme for CAV convoys.

title: Real-Time Multiple Vehicle Tracking Based on Multivariate Trajectory Prediction With Encoder--Decoder LSTM in Varying Lighting Conditions
authors: Igor Lashkov, Shanglian Zhou, Amanda Nitta, Guohui Zhang
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of multiple vehicles tracking in different complex road scenarios using traffic surveillance videos captured by cameras in varying lighting conditions. We formulate the multiple object tracking problem as a vehicle trajectory prediction, where the goal is to generate a future trajectory sequence of the object in real-time. We propose a lightweight online multi-object tracker based on the Encoder-Decoder LSTM architecture which analyzes patterns underlying the past object trajectory and estimates the vehicle’s motion in subsequent frames. The goal of the developed method is to establish correspondences between vehicle objects within a sequence of video frames. The use of object motion features promotes the generation of high-quality object trajectories and operation in a constantly changing traffic scene environment, with varying traffic flow density and illumination conditions. Tracking results from vehicle trajectories can be used efficiently to estimate the traffic flow parameters, such as traffic volume, vehicle presence, and vehicle movement speed, leading to effective intelligent transportation system (ITS) deployment. To demonstrate the efficiency of the developed approach, the extensive numerical evaluation carried out on multiple traffic scene datasets under diverse conditions demonstrates significant and robust results. During experiments, the tracking performance of the method is measured using specialized MOT metrics against existing tracking algorithms. Our developed approach is competitive against existing resource-intensive trackers and achieves high HOTA and MOTA metrics on publicly available MOT benchmarks. The designed tracking module with an incorporated LSTM network runs at a frequency of 16 Hz, enabling real-time traffic flow monitoring.

title: DriverPose: A Spatio-Temporal Convolutional Network for 3-D Driver Pose Estimation
authors: Weicheng Zheng, Ruisheng Yuan, Zhenyu Zhang, Hui Zhao, Chengjie Wang
abstract: In autonomous driving, the driver serves as the ultimate safety measure, making accurate pose estimation essential for effective driver monitoring systems. However, existing research on 3D human pose estimation has largely overlooked the important driving scenario. To address this, this work proposes DriverPose, a 3D driver pose estimation model based on a spatio-temporal convolutional network. DriverPose captures long-range sequential dependencies using temporal dilated convolutions and extracts spatial features through a novel graph attention mechanism. This mechanism integrates local and global information, uniquely embedding prior semantic knowledge of the driving context, such as kinematic hierarchies and common behavior patterns, to learn more relevant spatial relationships. Additionally, Conditional Batch Normalization with action type as a condition variable is applied after the graph convolution to adaptively handle different driving actions. To tackle the scarcity of training data in driving scenarios, a driving pose dataset named Human Driving-In-Vehicle (HDIV) with different driver body types and eight NDRTs is created. Experiments on the HDIV dataset and real-world driver videos show that DriverPose outperforms state-of-the-art methods in 3D driver pose estimation accuracy.

title: Cloud--Vehicle Collaborative Stability Control via Learning-Based Variable-Matrix Model Predictive Control With Region-of-Attraction Constraints
authors: Shengru Chen, Ronghui Zhang, Lin Zhang, Bolin Gao, Ying-En Ge, Lu Xiong
abstract: The rapid development of intelligent transportation systems, such as cloud-vehicle cooperative architectures, has opened new opportunities for enhancing vehicle safety control. Stability control for autonomous vehicles is a critical task in intelligent transportation systems. This paper presents a cloud-vehicle collaborative framework that integrates physics-based modeling with learning-based prediction to achieve stability-aware intelligent control. A Lyapunov-based sum-of-squares algorithm is developed for region-of-attraction estimation, explicitly incorporating a combined-slip LuGre tire model. These stability regions are embedded as constraints into a variable-matrix model predictive control scheme, ensuring region-of-attraction-constrained decision making. Meanwhile, a gated recurrent unit network, trained using nonlinear vehicle simulation data, predicts feedforward steering sequences to capture lateral-longitudinal coupling. The heavy computational tasks of network training and stability domain computation are offloaded to cloud computing, enabling efficient real-time execution onboard vehicles. Simulation results validate that the proposed approach improves both stability margins and trajectory tracking performance, highlighting its potential for future cooperative and safe autonomous driving systems.

title: Toward Closing the Sim-to-Real Gap for Autonomous Vehicles: A Physics-Guided Learning Approach for LiDAR Intensity Simulation
authors: Vivek Anand, Bharat Lohani, Rakesh Mishra, Vaibhav Kumar, Gaurav Pandey
abstract: LiDAR simulation is essential for developing and evaluating autonomous vehicles, particularly for testing perception algorithms in realistic, safety-critical environments such as urban driving. However, accurately simulating LiDAR intensity remains challenging, as simulations often fall short in capturing the complex interactions between the laser beam and objects, including surface reflectivity and incidence angle. Existing physics-based simulations often oversimplify these interactions, resulting in a substantial simulation-to-real gap. This paper introduces a novel architecture, the Physics-Informed Cycle-Consistent Generative Adversarial Network (PICGAN), which leverages cycle consistency and physics-based constraints to reduce this gap, enabling simulated point clouds to be assigned realistic intensities comparable to those from real-world LiDAR sensors. By integrating physical parameters of range, incidence angle, and material reflectance along with their interrelationships, PICGAN leverages unpaired real and simulated LiDAR data to more accurately replicate real-world intensity characteristics. PICGAN achieves a low KL divergence (e.g., 0.057 for cars) and a high average SSIM of 0.73 (±0.04), reflecting strong alignment with real LiDAR intensity. These enhancements also benefit downstream perception tasks in complex traffic scenes (up to 5.4% IoU improvement), highlighting the potential of our method to advance LiDAR-based perception for autonomous vehicles.

title: Unified Seamless Authenticated Key Agreement for Heterogeneous Train-to-Train Direct Communications Based on Distributed SDN
authors: Wenfang Zhang, Jiayi Zhou, Li Xue, Zhuoqun Yan, Muhammad Khurram Khan
abstract: Train-to-train (T2T) communication as a key technology of the next-generation train control system, is one of the hot topics in the field of rail transit today. However, since T2T communication is still in its infancy, existing research rarely considers the information security issues of T2T communication in heterogeneous network environments. This paper focuses on the authentication and key agreement between trains. Based on certificateless public key cryptography, this paper proposes a T2T communication authentication scheme in heterogeneous network environment without third-party online participation by introducing blockchain system and Software-Defined Networking (SDN) heterogeneous network management architecture. The scheme adopts a Train-to-Ground (T2G) communication approach to assist T2T communication, transferring the online dependency on the ground network to the front of T2T communication authentication, and uses a consortium blockchain as a trusted platform for global information flow. At the same time, it leverages the SDN controller to pre-distribute T2T communication authentication parameters. Security analysis shows that the proposed scheme can ensure the security of T2T communication in heterogeneous network environments and performs better than other existing schemes in terms of performance overhead and the ability to resist unknown attacks.

title: Beyond Safety: An Attention-Based Subjective--Objective Mapping Model for Autonomous Driving Intelligence Evaluation
authors: Yan Huang, Sihan Wang, Jian Sun, Ying Ni, Ye Tian
abstract: As autonomous driving systems advance beyond Level 3, traditional unidimensional evaluation methodologies are proving insufficient. A critical need exists for a reliable and trustworthy evaluation framework that aligns with human subjective judgment. Current approaches, however, often lack consensus on the relative importance of key performance dimensions and fail to capture how these evaluation priorities shift under varying scenario complexities. To address these gaps, a novel human-centered autonomous driving intelligence evaluation model, termed the Subjective-Objective Mapping Model (SOMM), is proposed. An evaluation index system is first established through the Delphi method, comprising five performance dimensions (safety, efficiency, comfort, regulatory compliance, traffic coordination) and one scenario dimension (scenario complexity). The SOMM is developed to map objective vehicle metrics onto subjective evaluation scores, demonstrating high predictive accuracy. Weight analysis quantifies the relative importance of performance dimensions, identifying safety and efficiency as the dominant factors in overall intelligence. Furthermore, a sensitivity analysis confirms that evaluation priorities are highly dynamic and scenario-dependent, shifting from traffic coordination and compliance in simple scenarios to safety and efficiency in complex environments. The proposed SOMM provides an accurate, interpretable, and dynamic evaluation framework that effectively quantifies autonomous driving intelligence by aligning it with human-centered criteria.

title: Cooperative Control of Heterogeneous Connected Vehicle Platoons: A Dynamic Event-Triggered Reinforcement Learning Approach
authors: Ke Wang, Junnan Zhang, Yichun Liu, Chaoxu Mu
abstract: With the increasing demand for connected and autonomous vehicle (CAV) platoons in the intelligent transportation system, optimizing communication resources while ensuring control performance has emerged as a critical challenge. To this end, this paper proposes a novel event-triggered reinforcement learning (ETRL) scheme for cooperative control of heterogeneous CAV platoons. The platooning control problem is first formulated as a multi-agent differential graphical game. Within this framework, each vehicle’s error dynamics and predefined performance functions depend solely on local and neighboring information. Then, a data-driven and off-policy integral reinforcement learning algorithm is developed to solve the coupled Hamilton-Jacobi equations which latently characterize the distributed optimal control policy. To further conserve communication resources, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism is introduced, and a single-critic network structure is used to implement the ETRL-based platooning control scheme. The stability and optimality of the vehicular platoon system are substantiated by strict theoretical analysis. Finally, through comprehensive simulations incorporating aggressive stop-and-go behaviors and periodic longitudinal disturbances, the effectiveness and superior performance of the proposed scheme are definitively validated against existing benchmark algorithms across multiple indicators.

title: Residual-Auxiliary Dual-Observer Architecture for Sensor Fault Detection in Networked Multi-Mobile Entity Systems
authors: Chengjun Ma, Lifeng Ma, Chen Gao
abstract: To address the evolving demands of future intelligent transportation systems, this paper conducts a comprehensive analysis and comparison of the operational characteristics among autonomous vehicles, autonomous metro trains, and formation-flying drone swarms. By identifying their dynamic commonalities, we propose the concept and dynamic model of a networked multi-mobile entity system (NMMES). Aiming at the challenges posed by unknown noise interference in sensor measurements of system velocity and displacement, a noise model decoupling method is introduced to handle colored correlated noise. Integrating the dynamic characteristics of NMMES, a Mahalanobis distance-based adaptive extended Kalman filtering algorithm with a forgetting factor is designed to achieve robust tracking of continuously varying system states. Furthermore, a residual-auxiliary dual-observer architecture is constructed, which leverages filtered results to reconstruct residual and auxiliary variables. This architecture enables sensor fault detection through adaptive error threshold configuration, while simultaneously enhancing system robustness against uncertainties. Simulation validation using a six-carriage metro train formation demonstrates the effectiveness and practical applicability of the proposed methodology in real-world transportation scenarios.

title: Automated Parking Planning Based on Safety Corridor Constraints and Parking Space Matching
authors: Kai Liu, Jian Zhou, Haoran Li, Youchen Tang, Jinsheng Xiao
abstract: The field of Automated Valet Parking (AVP) has garnered significant academic interest in recent years. However, traditional parking planning methods often struggle with maneuvering in compact spaces and large-scale environments. While effective for short-distance parking, these methods frequently encounter increased computational latency and sub-optimal path lengths in long-distance parking scenarios. Fundamentally, the inherent complexity of large-scale facilities extends beyond the practical capacity of conventional single-stage planners, necessitating a multi-stage strategy to balance global search efficiency with local maneuverability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a hierarchical parking planning framework using a decoupled two-stage approach. By integrating online safety corridor constraints with resolution-adaptive parking space matching, the method combines the global exploration of graph search with the local precision of optimization algorithms. The process employs a two-stage Hybrid A ${}^{\ast }$ strategy: global planning generates an initial trajectory in a low-resolution grid map, subsequently followed by local planning that refines the path to the target point within a high-resolution environment to ensure kinematic feasibility in constrained spaces. Experimental results indicate that this approach enhances algorithm efficiency by approximately 86.58% and reduces path length by an average of 21.68%. The proposed method improves adaptability to compact parking environments and reduces both generation time and path length in large-scale parking lots. Furthermore, the integration of adaptive safety corridor constraints and parking space matching enhances path safety and precision. The effectiveness of the method has been validated through real-world vehicle experiments, demonstrating its feasibility in practical AVP scenarios.

title: Vehicle-Cloud Cooperative Trajectory Planning via Switched Model Predictive Control for UGVs in Unstructured Transportation Environment
authors: Rong Wang, Dong Chen, Nan Li, Hang Gao, Yunfeng Hu, Yongfu Li, Hong Chen, Xun Gong
abstract: Recent advances in cloud computing and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication have created significant opportunities for intelligent transportation systems (ITS), particularly for tackling complex, high-level autonomous navigation tasks in unstructured environment that exceed the capabilities of onboard computing alone. However, the inherent uncertainty and latency of current wireless networks present a critical challenge to the safe deployment of cloud-based computation in safety-critical vehicular applications. To overcome these limitations, we propose a vehicle–cloud cooperative planning framework built on a parallel planning architecture. This approach simultaneously harnesses onboard and cloud resources: a lightweight linear model predictive control (LMPC) runs locally on the vehicle for fast, low-latency responses, while a more computationally intensive nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) executes on the cloud for enhanced foresight and optimality. A risk-based switching policy dynamically selects the optimal outputs of both planners, ensuring real-time adaptability and robustness in complex, unstructured traffic scenarios. Extensive simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed cooperative framework reduces collision probabilities by 32%–77% compared to standalone planners across diverse scenarios. The framework’s practical feasibility and real-world viability are further substantiated through experiments conducted on a purpose-built, scalable real-vehicle testing platform, marking a critical extension of our collaborative research from simulation to physical implementation.

title: H2C: Hippocampal Circuit-Inspired Continual Learning for Lifelong Trajectory Prediction in Autonomous Driving
authors: Yunlong Lin, Zirui Li, Guodong Du, Xiaocong Zhao, Cheng Gong, Xinwei Wang, Chao Lu, Jianwei Gong
abstract: Deep learning (DL) has shown state-of-the-art performance in trajectory prediction, which is critical to safe navigation in autonomous driving (AD). However, most DL-based methods suffer from catastrophic forgetting, where adapting to a new distribution may cause significant performance degradation in previously learned ones. Such an inability to retain learned knowledge limits their applicability in the real world, where AD systems need to operate across varying scenarios with dynamic distributions. As revealed by neuroscience, the hippocampal circuit plays a crucial role in memory replay, effectively reconstructing learned knowledge based on limited resources. Inspired by this, we propose a hippocampal circuit-inspired continual learning method (H2C) for trajectory prediction across varying scenarios. H2C retains prior knowledge by selectively recalling a small subset of learned samples. First, two complementary strategies are developed to select the subset to represent learned knowledge. Specifically, one strategy maximizes inter-sample diversity to represent the distinctive knowledge, and the other estimates the overall knowledge by equiprobable sampling. Then, H2C updates via a memory replay loss function calculated by these selected samples to retain knowledge while learning new data. Experiments based on various scenarios from the INTERACTION dataset are designed to evaluate H2C. Experimental results show that H2C reduces catastrophic forgetting of DL baselines by 22.71% on average in a task-free manner, without relying on manually informed distributional shifts. The implementation is available at https://github.com/BIT-Jack/H2C-lifelong

title: Learning-Based High-Level Decision Making for Abortable Overtaking in Autonomous Vehicles
authors: Ehsan Malayjerdi, Gokhan Alcan, Raivo Sell, Eshagh Kargar, Hatem Darweesh, Ville Kyrki
abstract: Autonomous vehicles are a growing technology that aims to enhance safety, accessibility, efficiency, and convenience through autonomous maneuvers ranging from lane change to overtaking. Overtaking is one of the most challenging maneuvers for autonomous vehicles, and current techniques for autonomous overtaking are limited to simple situations. This paper studies how to increase safety in autonomous overtaking by allowing the maneuver to be aborted. We propose a decision-making process based on a deep Q-Network to determine if and when the overtaking maneuver needs to be aborted. The proposed algorithm is empirically evaluated in simulation with varying traffic situations, indicating that the proposed method improves safety during overtaking maneuvers. Furthermore, the approach is demonstrated in real-world experiments using the autonomous shuttle iseAuto.

title: Time--Frequency Channel Prediction in Intelligent High-Speed Railway Communication Systems
authors: Chunchen Tan, Yuliang Cong, Fengye Hu
abstract: The successful development of the CR450 electric multiple unit marks a major technological breakthrough in the field of intelligent high-speed railway (HSR) systems. However, the operation of high-speed trains (HSTs) induces significant Doppler shifts, leading to severe degradation in communication efficiency. Channel prediction serves as an effective solution by predicting the future channel state information (CSI) to optimize transmission and improve communication performance. To this end, this paper proposes a prediction model based on a variable-aware time-frequency inverted Transformer (VATFIT), designed for the future intelligent HSR communication systems. Specifically, in the first stage, to address the challenge of limited CSI availability in HSR, a frequency dynamic propagation-graph (FDPG) simulation method for HSR CSI data generation is designed. This method constructs a time-frequency HSR CSI dataset and is validated against existing CSI generation methods. In the second stage, motivated by the inherent temporal and frequency-domain correlations in CSI, this paper incorporates both a cross-variable attention mechanism and a hybrid attention mechanism into the inverted Transformer (iTransformer) architecture to enhance inter-frequency interactions. Furthermore, normalized encoded frequency (NEF) as an auxiliary frequency-domain feature is introduced to further enhance the model’s multi-variable representation capacity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed VATFIT reduces the mean absolute error (MAE) by 2.8% compared to iTransformer, while maintaining computational complexity at a reasonable level.

title: RTRA: A Robust and Trustworthy Real-Time V2V Authentication Protocol Based on Geohash and Reputation Mechanisms
authors: Hang Yu, Hao Sun, Shuqin Luo, Ziyuan Pu
abstract: Authentication is a critical component in ensuring secure vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication within intelligent transportation systems. However, existing authentication protocols often overlook the dynamic characteristics of traffic accident scenarios, making it difficult to generate trustworthy incident reports and disseminate reliable warning messages in a timely manner. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a robust and trustworthy real-time V2V authentication protocol based on Geohash and reputation mechanisms (RTRA). The proposed protocol incorporates three key components: First, a Geohash-based mutual authentication and cross-domain authentication framework is developed to enable location-bound identity verification, key agreement, and alert message broadcasting. Second, a dynamic reputation feedback mechanism is introduced, adjusting the sender’s reputation based on receiving vehicles’ feedback on message authenticity and their own reputation, thereby enhancing communication trustworthiness. Finally, a dynamic pseudonym management mechanism is designed to protect vehicle privacy while supporting traceability and revocation of malicious entities. Theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed protocol significantly improves authentication reliability and message credibility, while achieving strong security and practical performance in safety-critical vehicular communication scenarios.

title: A Clone Selection-Based Algorithm for Railway Control Systems Checking Sequence Generation
authors: Yuchu Liao, Li He, Krishnan Guruvayur Venkateswaran, Yingcen Tee, Nicolas Dumler, Dimantha Gunawardana, Lei Chen
abstract: Software testing is crucial in verifying that system functionality meets specified requirements, especially in safety-critical railway control applications. This research employs Model-Based Testing to automate the generation of checking sequences for the Automatic Power Change-over system, leveraging a Python-based tool to create and refine test sequences from formalized UPPAAL models. Our approach integrates a clonal selection algorithm to inject diversity into the searching process, along with a reconstruction technique grounded in breadth-first search that preserves beneficial coverage paths, preventing coverage regression and ensuring more systematic exploration of complex state spaces. Experimental results show that transition coverage can be improved from an initial range of 50–60% to full transition coverage through iterative enhancements, requiring fewer refinements compared to purely random methods. This combination proves particularly effective for the Automatic Power Change-over system, which attained complete coverage with fewer iterations. These findings underscore the utility of structured mutation strategies and parameter optimization for achieving comprehensive coverage. Future work will investigate the integration of genetic algorithms to balance diversity and efficiency, as well as adopting more extensive coverage criteria suitable for train control systems. Converting these optimized checking sequences into executable test cases will further enhance safety and reliability in real-world operations.

title: A Reinforcement Learning-Based Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control Under False Data Injection Attacks
authors: Parisa Ansari Bonab, Arman Sargolzaei
abstract: Connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) are introduced to enhance the safety, efficiency, and mobility of transportation systems by leveraging advanced onboard sensors and wireless communication technologies. Cooperative adaptive cruise control (CACC), a fundamental application of CAVs, enhances adaptive cruise control (ACC) by treating multiple vehicles in close proximity as a platoon. Each vehicle within the platoon is equipped with a controller that leverages sensor-based measurements and vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication to maintain safe and optimal inter-vehicle spacing. Although this system has significant potential to enhance traffic safety and efficiency, it remains vulnerable to false data injection (FDI) attacks, which can compromise system safety. Since the FDI attack is unknown and nonlinear, the CACC should be able to estimate and mitigate it in real-time. There exist several techniques in the literature to detect and estimate FDI attacks in real-time. However, none of them provides an asymptotic coverage. To address this issue, this paper presents a novel adaptive critic control and FDI attack estimation design leveraging reinforcement learning and Lyapunov stability analysis to mitigate the adverse effects of FDI attacks and bounded disturbance. This method yields semi-global asymptotic stability results. Theoretical analysis and simulation results are provided to illustrate the performance of the developed controller.

title: Integrity Monitoring of GNSS Railway Localization With a Map-Based Multipath Error Model
authors: Florian Robl, Omar Garcia Crespillo
abstract: Satellite-based navigation can enable in the near future interoperable railway signaling capabilities and improve railway traffic management. For railway safety functions, the use of global navigation satellite system (GNSS) has to be proven safe for the specific operational environments. This is, however, still a challenge due to the presence of local GNSS errors, such as multipath, which are difficult to model. One of the main reasons is its strong dependency with the surroundings along the tracks that creates a high variability of the multipath error experienced by GNSS receiver at every point of the railway line. This work proposes a methodology to model the train GNSS multipath error by creating a digital map of multipath information. The information in the map provides a parametric and conservative description of the error that can be used by the GNSS receiver. The map-based error model is constructed by applying error overbounding techniques over empirical data collected along the tracks. The resulting error map is then integrated and evaluated in an advanced receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (ARAIM) algorithm adapted to the railway environment and that provides a position solution along with associated integrity bounds. The experimental results based on real railway data demonstrate the capability of this methodology and models to provide a reliable multipath error description for train localization while maintaining high availability.

title: Edge Case Detection in Automated Driving: Methods, Challenges, and Future Directions
authors: Saeed Rahmani, Sabine Rieder, Erwin de Gelder, Marcel Sonntag, Jorge Lorente Mallada, Sytze Kalisvaart, Vahid Hashemi, Bart van Arem, Simeon C. Calvert
abstract: Automated vehicles (AVs) promise to enhance transportation safety and efficiency. However, ensuring their reliability in real-world conditions remains challenging, particularly due to rare and unexpected situations known as edge cases. While numerous approaches exist for detecting edge cases, a comprehensive survey reviewing these techniques is lacking. This paper bridges this gap by presenting a hierarchical review and systematic classification of edge case detection and assessment methodologies. Our classification is structured on two levels: first, by AV modules, including perception and trajectory-related (encompassing prediction, planning, and control) subsystems; and second, by underlying methodologies and theories guiding these techniques. Furthermore, we introduce “knowledge-driven” approaches, which complement data-driven methods by leveraging expert insights and domain knowledge to identify cases absent in training datasets. We then examine techniques and metrics for evaluating edge case detection methods, including detection performance, practical deployment (e.g., computational overhead), and domain-specific measures (e.g., crash rates and severity analysis). We conclude by highlighting key challenges for edge case detection, including data availability and quality issues, validation and interpretability limitations, the simulation-to-real gap, and computational constraints. The hierarchical classification and review of methods and assessment techniques in this survey enable modular and targeted testing frameworks by guiding the selection of detection methods for specific AV subsystems while considering methodological principles. It also supports practical testing by facilitating scenario generation in simulation and focused subsystem validation in the real world.

title: A Motion Planning Control Strategy for Autonomous Vehicles Considering Driving Style Personalization and Optimal Energy Consumption
authors: Fuhao Zuo, Xia Li, Benxue Liu
abstract: This paper proposes a novel motion planning algorithm based on model predictive control (MPC) and fuzzy logic to address the coordinated motion planning problem in terms of optimal energy consumption while maintaining specific driving style. The MPC controller based on the linear time-varying (LTV) vehicle dynamics model is constructed to deal with the calculation of trajectory tracking accuracy, while the optimal energy consumption term is also integrated into the evaluation function. To transform the non-convex optimization problem into quadratic programming (QP), the tracking error is further linearized. Noting that differentiated control objectives lead to potential abnormal acceleration fluctuations, the weight adjustment mechanism is adopted to handle the adjustment of vehicle’s dynamic behavior. In the process of adaptive weight configuration, the fuzzy logic controller based on driving intention and deviation level is designed to achieve the goal of maintaining the preset driving style. Therefore, by leveraging the correlation between driving style definition and acceleration/deceleration decisions, the trade-off problem in motion planning and the riding comfort issue can be addressed simultaneously. Moreover, the improved algorithm under three different driving styles and the original MPC planner are tested and compared in the typical cornering scenario. By introducing the optimal energy consumption term at the cost of a 4.08% extension in scenario passage time, the proposed algorithm achieves up to a 29.76% reduction in trajectory deviation and a 38.89% decrease in approximate driving energy consumption. Visual analysis of driving objectives’ trade-off further indicates that different driving style presets lead to distinct optimization potentials, while trajectory tracking still plays a dominant role in the overall control objectives.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Cooperation Scheduling Strategy for Single-Route Battery Electric Bus Fleets Considering Battery Capacity Decay and Nonlinear Charging
authors: Qiang Feng, Yu Zhou, Honghai Li, Rui Feng, Bin Yu
abstract: The scheduling problem of battery electric buses (BEBs) has been widely studied. However, most existing work focuses only on either operation or charging. In reality, these two aspects are interdependent and should be considered from a lifecycle perspective. This study proposes a cooperative scheduling strategy for BEB fleets on a single bus route. The strategy addresses opportunity charging under a limited charging infrastructure. It dynamically generates operation and charging decisions based on real-time system states. The goal is to reduce the impact of uneven terminal arrival times and mitigate battery aging. Both the nonlinear charging behavior and battery aging are considered in the charging plan. The BEB work cycle is modeled as two interrelated Markov Decision Processes (MDPs): one for operation and one for charging. A deep reinforcement learning framework, called the Double-SAC-Combination Framework, is used to solve the model. It integrates the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) and Discrete SAC algorithms. The model is validated using real-world data from Beijing Bus Line 44 (inner loop). Results show that the proposed strategy reduces daily battery capacity degradation by 8.5% to 33.3% compared to a no-control baseline. The best performance is achieved when the headway is 6 minutes, speed is 25 km/h, fleet size is 35, and there are 4 charging piles. Sensitivity analyses are conducted on BEB load differences, driving speed, headway, number of charging piles, fleet size, route length, and battery capacity.

title: Risk Occupancy: A New and Efficient Paradigm Through Vehicle-Road-Cloud Collaboration
authors: Jiaxing Chen, Wei Zhong, Bolin Gao, Yifei Liu, Hengduo Zou, Jiaxi Liu, Yanbo Lu, Jin Huang, Zhihua Zhong
abstract: This paper proposes a novel 4D risk occupancy (RiskOcc) perception paradigm under the Vehicle-Road-Cloud integrated architecture, which unifies object detection and local mapping into a single representation spanning four dimensions: road-surface x and y coordinates, risk, and time. Distinct from conventional grid occupancy and risk field methods, this paradigm adopts an anchor-node-based perception approach with a concise yet reliable risk quantification scheme, enabling flexible and accurate capture of static and dynamic object occupancy states at current and future time steps, with per-occupancy-unit risk quantification. Compared with 3D-Occ, the proposed RiskOcc requires only one layer of data volume and achieves higher perceptual computational efficiency. Visualizations of risk occupancy perception results are presented based on the DAIR-V2X dataset, and a path planning method is developed to verify the usability of the risk occupancy map. Experimental results show that at an initial braking speed of 8 m/s, the model improves safety redundancy by 12.5% and reduces average deceleration by 5.41%, enhancing both safety and comfort. In summary, this study introduces a novel perception paradigm for intelligent connected vehicle (ICV), providing a compact and interpretable risk representation for cooperative perception and downstream planning in ICV systems.

title: Class-Enhanced Multi-Sampling and Multi-Level Graph Attention for 3-D Object Detection
authors: Xiangyang Wu, Jitao Pan, Qinglong Jiao, Kailun Qian, Zhen Liu
abstract: Three-dimensional object detection is a key component of the perception module in autonomous driving systems. Compared to camera images, LiDAR point clouds provide richer spatial information, such as detailed structural and geometric cues of objects. However, existing 3D object detection methods face two major challenges: 1) loss of critical information due to downsampling or convolution operations, leading to missed detections, and 2) insufficient exploitation of contextual information around objects, resulting in inaccurate bounding box regression. These problems are particularly severe when detecting sparse point cloud objects that are distant or occluded. To address these issues, we propose two novel modules applicable to both point-based and voxel-based detection frameworks: the Class-Enhanced Multi-Sampling (CEMS) module and the Multi-Level Graph Attention (MLGA) module. The CEMS module employs an iterative class-aware sampling and semantic interpolation strategy to achieve more precise downsampling of critical information, while the MLGA module integrates both intra-layer and cross-layer graph attention to capture local geometric structures around objects as well as inter-object relationships, thereby enhancing the representation of key features. Comprehensive evaluations on multiple datasets, including ONCE, Waymo, and nuScenes, demonstrate that the proposed modules can consistently improve the detection performance across various network architectures while maintaining high inference efficiency.

title: Secure State Estimation of Nonlinear Autonomous Marine Vehicle Systems With Location-Varying Sparse Attacks
authors: Qingdong Sun, Guang-Hong Yang
abstract: This paper investigates the secure state estimation problem of autonomous marine vehicles (AMVs) under location-varying sparse attacks and external disturbances, where the AMV is modeled as a continuous-time T-S fuzzy system. To effectively suppress destructive attacks, a redundant-channel transmission mechanism is adopted to transmit the measurable output information, and a necessary and sufficient condition for the reconstruction of the measurable outputs is given. Furthermore, the generalized inverse technique is applied to transform the original system into a form that is not affected by external disturbances, along with a necessary and sufficient condition for the observability of the transformed system. Then, an observer is designed using the reconstructed measurement output signals and the observable transformed system, which differs from the existing methods in that its estimation error can converge to zero in a finite time. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the designed observer are verified through simulation experiments.

title: Deep Learning-Based Monitoring of Flight Path Deviations for eVTOL Aircraft: A Gated Recurrent Unit Model Perspective
authors: Jeongmin Kim, Peng Wei, Kyowon Song
abstract: —Urban Air Mobility (UAM) is transitioning from initial pilot-controlled deployments toward UAM Maturity Level 4, which envisions full autonomy in dense aerial environments. In such highly automated systems, even minor trajectory deviations can escalate into critical safety hazards. However, existing frameworks often lack the real-time precision and robustness required to detect these anomalies early, especially when faced with unexpected system disturbances or external interference. This study develops an artiﬁcial intelligence (AI)-based predictive model to identify deviations from planned ﬂight paths and facilitate timely air tra ﬃ c control alerts. Using high-ﬁdelity X-Plane simulations of the ALIA-250, an electric vertical take-o ﬀ and landing (eVTOL) aircraft along Han River VFR routes, we collected autopilot data to train and compare Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) architectures. The GRU model demonstrated superior performance, achieving the lowest prediction error and 100% availability for a 3-second-ahead forecast. Furthermore, the model’s robustness was validated using synthetic ﬂight data simulating various system failures and cyberattacks, conﬁrming its potentialto provide early hazard warnings andsupporttransitions to manual controlwithin a simulated environment. These ﬁndingsdemonstrate the feasibility of AI-basedanomaly detectionas a proof-of-concept framework for trajectory monitoring in future UAM operations, with further validation under real-world conditions required before operational deployment.

title: RSTGCN: Railway-Centric Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network for Train Delay Prediction
authors: Koyena Chowdhury, Paramita Koley, Abhijnan Chakraborty, Saptarshi Ghosh
abstract: Accurate prediction of train delays is critical for efficient railway operations. While earlier approaches have largely focused on forecasting the exact delays of individual trains, studies on station-level delay prediction are somewhat sparse. To address this gap, we propose the Railway-centric Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (RSTGCN), designed to forecast average arrival delays of all the incoming trains at a particular station for a particular time period. Our approach incorporates several architectural innovations and novel feature integrations, including train frequency-aware spatial attention, which significantly enhance predictive performance. To support this effort, we curate and release a comprehensive dataset for the entire Indian Railway Network (IRN), spanning 4,735 stations across 17 zones - the largest and most diverse railway network studied to date. We conduct extensive experiments using multiple state-of-the-art baselines, demonstrating consistent improvements across standard metrics. Specifically, RSTGCN outperforms the best baseline by 18% in MAE, 14% in MAPE, and 1-8% in RMSE on the IRN.

title: Learn2Drive: A Neural Network-Based Framework for Socially Compliant Automated Vehicle Control
authors: Yuhui Liu, Samannita Halder, Shian Wang, Tianyi Li
abstract: This study introduces a novel control framework for adaptive cruise control (ACC) in automated driving, leveraging neural networks and physics-informed constraints. As automated vehicles (AVs) adopt advanced features like ACC, transportation systems are becoming increasingly intelligent and efficient. However, existing AV control strategies primarily focus on optimizing the performance of individual vehicles or platoons, often neglecting their interactions with human-driven vehicles (HVs) and the broader impact on traffic flow. This oversight can exacerbate congestion and reduce overall system efficiency. To address this critical research gap, we propose a neural network-based, socially compliant AV control framework that incorporates social value orientation (SVO). This framework enables AVs to account for their influence on HVs and traffic dynamics. By leveraging AVs as mobile traffic regulators, the proposed approach promotes adaptive driving behaviors that reduce congestion, improve traffic efficiency, and lower energy consumption. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in adapting to varying traffic conditions, thereby enhancing system-wide efficiency. Specifically, when the AV's control mode shifts from prioritizing its own energy conservation to optimizing collective traffic flow efficiency, the controlled AV proactively adapts its acceleration profile. This prosocial behavior yields at least a 38.39\% improvement in the average speed of downstream vehicles and effectively dampens traffic oscillations, demonstrating significant enhancements in system-wide dynamics. The implementation code is available https://github.com/lilab2024/Learn2Drive-SVO_v1.git.
